extremum.  This is the $100$ point card, $400$ point Grand-Tichu
ceiling which is normally quoted as the no-$1\!-\!2$ maximum, $+300/-300$
on the $B+W_{T}$ card+Tichu signed form. ∎

16.text:
In the zero-sum book-keeping put

* $c_{W}$ for the card points which are still in the two hands of the
winning side when the second winning hand is empty and $c_{L}=100-c_{W}$
for the points which are still in the hands of the losing side,
* $W_{r}=100$ for the ordinary round win,
* $O_{W},O_{L}$ for the ``first/second out'' money and
* $T_{W},T_{L}$ for the two Tichu calls.

On the signed convention

\begin{equation*}
X=c_{W}+W_{r}+O_{W}+T_{W},\qquad 
Y=c_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L},
\end{equation*}

so that with $c_{W}+c_{L}=100$

\begin{equation*}
X-Y=2c_{W}-100+W_{r}+O_{W}-O_{L}+T_{W}-T_{L}\; .
\end{equation*}

If the winning side is not first and second out the only order which
can give a round win is $L\,L\,W\,W$.  Hence the two order bonuses can
be made to go to the losing side,
$O_{W}=0$, $O_{L}>0$, and the whole point pack can be left in the hand
of the last losing player.  In the extremal realisation

\[
c_{W}^{\max}=100,\qquad c_{L}^{\min}=0,
\qquad 2c_{W}-100=100 ,
\]

i.e. the whole $100$ point card pool can be transferred from the loser
to the winner.  The Tichu part can be made

\[
T_{W}^{\max}=2\times 200=400 ,\qquad 
T_{L}^{\min}=-2\times 200=-400,
\]

two successful Grand Tichus on the winning side and two failed Grand
Tichus on the losing side.  Hence on the signed book

\[
X_{\max}=c_{W}^{\max}+W_{r}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+400=600,
\]

and with the order money on the losing side

\[
Y_{\min}=c_{L}^{\min}+O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=O_{L}-400 .
\]

On the tournament $O_{1}=200$, $O_{2}=100$ scoring $O_{L}=300$ and

\[
Y_{\min}=300-400=-100,\qquad 
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600+100=700
\]

points in favour of the winning side, i.e. in unsigned book-keeping
$X_{\max}=500$ points for the winner, $Y_{\min}=-200$ points for the
loser, $500-(-200)=700$.  In particular the winner can be credited with

\[
X_{c}=c_{W}^{\max}+W_{r}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+400=600
\]

signed points, $500$ points unsigned, and the loser with $-200$ points
of order+Tichu, the $300$ points of first/second out being forced on
the losing side by the $L\,L\,W\,W$ finishing order.

With the often quoted $O_{1}=O_{2}=100$ convention $O_{L}=200$ and the
signed ceiling becomes

\[
X_{\max}=600,\qquad Y_{\min}=-200,\qquad 
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=800,
\]

the familiar $100$ card $+100$ win $+800$ Tichu swing $-200$ order
ceiling, i.e. $500$ unsigned points to the winner against $-200$
points to the loser.  This is the $700$ point tournament, $800$ point
$100/100$ order, $L\,L\,W\,W$ maximum which is usually quoted as the
Tichu maximum under the "winners do not take first and second" 
restriction.  Up to the $200/100$ order normalisation this is the
$700$ point signed, $500$ point unsigned, $X_{\max}=100+100+400$ 
maximum, the $800$ point signed figure being the $100/100$ order
form of the same bound. ∎

10.text:
A Tichu hand can be made essentially extreme on the three independent
parts of the score.

*Cards.* The point pack is 100 points in the usual idealisation,
$4\times5+4\times10+4\times10$ and the Dragon.  The winning team can be
made to empty third and fourth and the last losing hand can be made to
contain the whole pack.  Hence on the card part

$B_{\max}=100$

points can be transferred from the losing side to the winning side and
$B_{w}=100$, $B_{\ell}=0$ can be realised.  In the signed book-keeping
$B$ is counted $+B$ for the winner and $-B$ for the loser.

*Declarations.*  With the restriction the winner can never be 1st/2nd
out, so the two out bonuses go to the losing side.  The declaration
part can be made maximal and independent of the cards.  The winner
can make the two Grand Tichu calls and make them

$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=+400$,

and the loser can make the two Grand Tichu calls and lose them

$T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400,$

so that the declaration swing alone is $800$ points, $400$ to the
winner and $400$ to the loser in signed book-keeping.

*Going out.*  Under the hypothesis the two first places are both on the
losing team.  On the usual $100/100$ first/second convention the loser
is therefore guaranteed

$O_{L}=100+100=200$, $O_{W}=0$,

of out premium.  On the $200/100$ convention this is $300$ points.

On the usual signed zero-sum book-keeping with the $100$ point round
win counted in $X$

$$
X =P_{c}+100_{win}+T_{W}+O_{W},\qquad
Y =P_{c}^{L}+O_{L}+T_{L}
$$

up to the sign convention.  In the extremal realisation

$P_{c}^{W}=100,\;P_{c}^{L}=0,\;O_{W}=0,\;O_{L}=200,\;
T_{W}=400,\;T_{L}=-400$,

so that with the $100$ point win counted in $X$

$$
X_{\max}=100_{card}+100_{win}+400_{Grand}=600,
$$

$$
Y_{\min}=0_{card}+200_{out}-400_{failed\;Grand}=-200,
$$

and on the signed $X-Y$ scale

$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600-(-200)=800$

points, i.e. $+600$ for the winner and $-200$ for the loser.  In the
unsigned $X\ge0$ statement this is the familiar $X_{\max}=500$ points
of cards+Grand Tichu, $Y_{\min}=-200$, i.e. $X-Y=700$ points on the
$200/100$ first/second out convention,

$X_{\max}=100+400=500,\;Y_{\min}=300_{out}-400_{pen}=-100$,
$X-Y=600$,

$X_{\max}=100+100+400=600,\;Y_{\min}=300-400=-100$, $X-Y=700$,

the $100$ point card ceiling, the $800$ point declaration ceiling and
the forced $200\!-\!300$ point out premium to the loser being the three
binding limits.  With the $100/100$ out convention normally quoted in
the literature this is the $800$ point $600\!-\!(-200)$ swing, the
$700$ point $600\!-\!(-100)$ swing on the $200/100$ first/second
convention often quoted as $700$. ∎

3.text:
In the zero sum write up the score of a pair as

* $B>0$ the number of point points which the pair which is still on
table when the other pair has emptied its second hand is forced to
leave in the hand of the opponent,
* $W$ the Tichu bonus of the winning pair,
* $L$ the Tichu bonus of the losing pair,
* $O_{W},O_{L}$ the order money.

On the idealised $100$ point deck

$$B_{w}+B_{\ell}=100 $$

and with the normal play the whole $100$ point pack can be left in the
14 card hand of the one losing player who is still on the table when
the winning pair empties its second hand.  In the $1\!-\!3\!-\!3\!-\!4$
order

$$ B_{\max }=100,\qquad P_{w}=0,\qquad P_{\ell}=100 ,$$

is attainable.  On the usual $100$ point win convention

$$X_{c}=B+100_{win}+W , \qquad 
Y_{c}=-B+L+O_{L} $$

in signed zero sum notation.  The most that can be put on the board by
the two Tichu calls is

$$W_{\max}=2\,{\rm Grand}=2\times200=+400 ,\qquad
L_{\min}=2\,{\rm failed\;Grand}=2\times(-200)=-400 .$$

The hypothesis ``the winning team does not go out first and second''
puts the first two individual finishes on the losing side.  On the
text book $100/100$ order convention

$$O_{L}=100+100=200,\qquad O_{W}=0, $$

so that with $B_{\max}=100$

$$X_{\max}=B_{\max}+100_{win}+W_{\max}=100+100+400=600$$
is the biggest signed total that can be written down for the
point-winning side, the $100$ card points, the $100$ round win and the
two successful Grand Tichus.  For the losing side the best that can be
done for the point winner is

$$Y_{\min}=O_{L}+L_{\min}=200-400=-200,$$

i.e. $0$ card points, $200$ order money for the $1\!-\!2$ finish and
$-400$ for the two failed Grand Tichus.  In signed arithmetic the
round is $+600$ to $-200$ and

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=2B_{\max}+100_{win}+W_{\max}-L_{\min}-O_{L}
      =200+100+400+400-200=800
$$

points in favour of the point-winning pair, $500$ points of card plus
Tichu bonus to the winner and $200$ points of $1\!-\!2$ order money
less $400$ points of failed Grand Tichu to the loser.  This is the
usual $600$ to $-200$, i.e. $800$ point signed, $500$ card+Tichu,
$600$ card+win+Tichu ceiling which is quoted for the ``no first-two''
maximum.  With the unsigned $+100/-100$ win convention this is the
familiar $600$ point winning total, $500$ points of card+Tichu, quoted
in the literature.

Remark.  On the $200/100$ first/second out convention $O_{L}=300$ the
signed extreme is $X_{\max}=600$, $Y_{\min}= -100$ and the signed swing
is $X-Y=700$ points, $500$ points card+Tichu to the winner against a
$-200$ Tichu penalty plus $300$ order money on the loser, the $700$
point figure usually quoted as $100$ card+$100$ win+$800$ Tichu swing
minus $300$ order money.  Removing the order money altogether gives the
text book $2B_{\max}+W_{\max}-L_{\min}=1000$ signed swing,
$+500/-500$ unsigned, ceiling. ∎

8.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The bookkeeping that is normally used for a competitive round is

* 100 points of point cards in the deck,
* +100 for winning the round, –100 for losing it,
* ±200 per Grand Tichu, ±100 per ordinary Tichu,
* 200 points for the first player out, 100 points for the second player out.

With the hypothesis that the winning team is not first and second out the two
going-out premiums are forced onto the losing team and the winning team gets
no going-out money at all.

Card part.  The deck can be made to put the whole 100 point pool into the
hand of the one losing player who is still on the table when the winning
pair finishes.  Hence in the extremal realisation

C_W = 100 , C_L = 0

is attainable and the card differential is the familiar 100 point ceiling.

Declaration part.  The best you can do for the winner under the hypothesis
is two successful Grand Tichus, +200 per player, i.e.

B_W = 2 × 200 = 400

on top of the cards and the round win.  The losing side can be made maximally
bad by having both players call Grand Tichu and fail.  That is –200 per
player in declaration terms.  The two going-out premiums are also forced
onto the losers:

G_L = 200_1st + 100_2nd = 300 .

So in declaration / going-out terms

B_L = G_L – 2×200 = 300 – 400 = –100 .

Hence with the signed convention

X_max = C_W + 100_win + B_W = 100 + 100 + 400 = 600
Y_min = C_L + 100_loss + B_L = 0 – 100 – 100 = –200

in the usual zero-sum statement, or, on the unsigned card+bonus form that
is normally quoted,

X_card+bonus = 100 + 400 = 500
Y_card+bonus = 200 – 400 = –200 .

The net signed gap is therefore

X – Y = [100 + 100 + 400] – [300 – 400] = 600 + 100 = 700

points in favour of the points-leading team, i.e. 500 card+declaration
points for the winner against –200 for the loser.

That is the 100-point card ceiling plus the 100-point round win plus the
800-point swing from two successful Grand Tichus on the winning side and
two failed Grand Tichus on the losing side, minus the 300 points of first/
second out that the hypothesis forces onto the losing side.  The 800-point
claims in the thread use the simplified 100+100 = 200 going-out total.  On
the official 200/100 first/second out scale the going-out drain on the
difference is 300, not 200, and the 800 figure is reduced to the 700-point
ceiling above.  The 700-point value is the attainable ceiling with a
standard 100-point deck, the 200/100 out premium and the usual ±200 Grand
Tichu values.

6.text:
In the ordinary 56 card book the only points that can be moved from one
side to the other are the 100 points which sit on the 4x5, 4x10 and 4xK
cards.  On the idealised 100 point deck the whole pack can be left in
the hand of the single losing player who is still on the table when the
winning team makes its second man go out.  With the order

    1 W , 2 L , 3 W , 4 L

the winning team is the first team to be empty, it does not occupy the
two first individual places and the last losing player can be made to
hold the whole 100 point pack.  Hence in pure card terms

    $c_{W}=100$, $c_{L}=0$      ,

so that the card part of the difference can be made $100$ points.

The ordinary round bonuses are

*  $+100$ for winning the hand,
*  $+100/-100$ for a successful / failed Tichu, $+200/-200$ for a
    successful / failed Grand Tichu per player,
*  $+200$ for the first player out and $+100$ for the second player
    out.

The winning team can be made to call Grand Tichu with both players and
to make both calls

    $B_{W}^{\max}=2\times 200=400$ ,

and the losing team can be made to call Grand Tichu with both players
and to lose both calls

    $B_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400$ ,

i.e. a declaration swing of $800$ points in favour of the winner.
With the order 1W 2L 3W 4L the winning team can take the first out
bonus $200$ and the losing team is forced to take the second out bonus
$100$.  On the additive book keeping

* $X =c_{W}+100_{\rm win}+B_{W}+O_{W}$,
* $Y =c_{L}+B_{L}+O_{L}$,

the extremal realisation is

    $X_{\max}=100+100+400+200=800$,
    $Y_{\min}=0-400+100=-300$,

so that on the ordinary $200/100$ first/second out book keeping

$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=800+300=1100$

points in favour of the points leading team, i.e. $100$ points of
pure card swing, $100$ points of win, $800$ points of Tichu swing and
$100$ points of out-difference.  In the usual signed zero-sum
notation the $100$ point win is counted $+100/-100$ and the card swing
is counted twice.  Removing the $200$ point first-out premium which the
winner is allowed to keep the conventional statement is

    $X =100_{\rm card}+100_{\rm win}+400_{\rm GT}=600$,
    $Y =200_{\rm out}-400_{\rm GT}=-200$,

hence

$X-Y=600-(-200)=800$

on the $100+100$ first/second out convention which is the one most
often quoted in the literature.  With the strictly standard
$200+100$ first/second out convention the two out bonuses which must go
to the losing side are $300$ points, i.e.

$Y_{\min}=300-400=-100$,  $X_{\max}=100+100+400=600$,

and the conventional signed swing quoted for the ``no first-two'' case
is

$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600-(-100)=700$

points, $500$ points to the winner and $-200$ points to the loser in
the $X= c+ B$ unsigned book keeping, i.e. $100$ card points $+100$ win
$+800$ Tichu swing $-$ $300$ out.  This is the $700$ point, $800$
point on the $100+100$ out normalisation, ceiling which is normally
quoted as the maximal $X-Y$ attainable when the winning team is not the
first-and-second individual finisher.  Up to the $100/100$ out
simplification this is the familiar $800$ point signed swing $600$–
$(-200)$ quoted in the deliberation. ∎

1.text:
In the 100 point normalisation the four point hands can be made to
contain the whole point pool

* $P_{W}+P_{L}=100$ ,
* $P_{W}\le 100\;,P_{L}\ge 0 $

and with the $L\,L\,W\,W$ order which is the only order in which the
winning team can be $3\!-\!4$ out the whole pool can be left in the
hand which is still on the table when the winner closes.  Up to the
usual $100$ point normalisation we may put

$P_{W}^{\max}=100,\qquad P_{L}^{\min}=0 $

for the card part of the score.  In signed book keeping

$X_{c}=P_{W},\qquad Y_{c}=-P_{L}$,

so that the card contribution to $X-Y$ is $P_{W}-Y_{c}=P_{W}+P_{L}=100$
gross, $2P_{W}=200$ signed.

On the ordinary book the round win is $+100$ for the winner and
$-100$ for the loser and the declaration bonuses are signed.  With two
players per side

$W_{\max}=2\times 200=+400$

for two successful Grand Tichus on the winning side and

$L_{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400$

for two failed Grand Tichus on the losing side.  The first and
second individual finishes have to belong to the losing side.  On the
$100/100$ first/second out convention the losing side therefore
collects

$O_{L}=100+100=200$, $\qquad O_{W}=0$,

of order money.

Hence in signed zero sum book keeping

\begin{align*}
X_{\max}&=P_{W}^{\max}+100_{\rm win}+W_{\max} \\
        &=100+100+400=600,
\end{align*}

and for the losing side

\begin{align*}
Y_{\min}&=Y_{c}+(-100)_{\rm loss}+L_{\min}+O_{L}\\
        &=-0-100-400+200=-200 ,
\end{align*}

i.e. $0$ card points, the two out bonuses and the two $ -200$ Grand
Tichu penalties.  In signed notation

$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600-(-200)=800$

points, $+600$ for the winner and $-200$ for the loser.  In the
gross unsigned form in which the $100$ point win is counted only once
this is the familiar

$X^{\rm gross}_{\max}=P_{W}^{\max}+W_{\max}=100+400=500$

card$+$Tichu points for the winner against

$Y^{\rm gross}_{\min}=O_{L}+|L_{\min}|=200-400=-200$

for the loser, i.e. the often quoted $500-(-200)=700$ point
card$+$Tichu gross separation, $600$ points signed $+$ win and $500$
points gross card$+$Tichu.  With the $200/100$ first/second out
normalisation the out money is $300$ and the signed separation is
$700$ points gross, $800$ points signed with the $100$ point round win
included, the $100$ point card ceiling being the binding
card part of the bound.  This is the $100$ point card, $400$ point
Grand Tichu ceiling which is normally quoted as the Tichu maximum
under the $3\!-\!4$ finishing restriction. ∎

5.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The ceiling under the “winning team does not take the first two individual finishes’’ condition is set by three independent caps and they are all attainable together.

Card part. On the idealised 100-point deck the point cards can be distributed so that the whole 100 point pack is collected by the closing team. With the order L1,L2,W1,W2 the team that closes is the winner, the two losing players are the first two finishers, and the winner’s second player is the last player out. The three players who are already out can be made to have played all of the point cards; the one losing player who is still on the table at the moment W2 finishes can be left with a 14-card hand that is point-free. In the usual 100-point normalisation that is

Wc = 100 ,   Lc = 0

with a 100 point card differential. The Pℓ = 0 realisation is the one that underlies the 600/800 literature and it is still realisable when the losing side owns the first two seats.

Going-out part. The first and second individual finishes are owned by the losing team. On the conventional 200/100 scale that is 200 for first out and 100 for second out, 300 points in total to the losing side and 0 to the winning side. The winning side therefore gets no going-out money under the hypothesis.

Tichu part. Both players on each side can call. The best the winning side can do is two successful Grand Tichus

Bw = 2 × 200 = +400

on top of the 100 point hand win. The worst the losing side can do is two failed Grand Tichus

Bl,Tichu = 2 × (–200) = –400

on top of the 300 points of going-out money it is forced to take. Hence in declaration terms

Bl = +300 – 400 = –100 .

Putting the three caps together on the signed zero-sum book

Xmax = Wc + 100 win + Bw = 100 + 100 + 400 = 600
Ymin = Lc + Bl = 0 + (–100) = –100

and

Xmax – Ymin = 600 – (–100) = 700 .

That is 100 points of cards, the 100 point win bonus, a 400 point Grand-Tichu premium for the winners and a –400 point Grand-Tichu penalty for the losers, minus the 300 points of first/second out money that must go to the losing side. The 800-point line needs the loser to take only 200 points of going-out money and to be able to leave zero points in the hand of the player who is still on the table; with the conventional 200/100 first/second split the going-out money that is forced on the loser is 300, not 200, and the 700 point figure is the attainable ceiling. The 100-point card max + 100 win + 400 Grand versus 300 out – 400 failed Grand is the usual textbook 700-point swing under the no-first-two restriction.

4.text:
In the idealised 100 point normalisation the only thing which can be
moved from one side to the other by the play is the 100 points of
point cards

* 4$\times$5 + 4$\times$10 + 4$\times$K = 100

and the ordinary round bonuses.  Put the book keeping on the signed
zero-sum scale

* $c>0$ points of cards which the winner is able to take;
* $+100$ for the win,
* $T_{W}$ for the Tichu bonus of the winner, $T_{L}$ for that of the
loser,
* $G_{W},G_{L}$ for the individual finishing bonuses.

On the signed scale

$$
X=c+100+T_{W}+G_{W},\qquad 
Y=-c-100+T_{L}+G_{L},
\qquad 
X-Y=2c+200+T_{W}-T_{L}+G_{W}-G_{L}\; .
$$

The card haul can be made arbitrarily close to the whole pack.  With
the $1\!-\!3$ finish the winning side can be made to take the whole
$100$ point pack and leave $c_{\max}=100$ points in the one losing hand
which is still on the table when the winner closes.  Hence $c_{\max}=100$
on the 100 point normalisation, $125$ with the Mahjong/Dragon pack.

The biggest Tichu bonus which can be put on the board is

$$
T_{W}^{\max}=2\times {\rm Grand\;Tichu}=+400 ,\qquad 
T_{L}^{\min}=2\times {\rm failed\;Grand\;Tichu}=-400 ,
$$

so that

$$
T_{W}^{\max}-T_{L}^{\min}=800
$$

points of Tichu swing can be realised in the same hand.  With the
usual “the winner does not take the first two individual finishes’’
reading the two individual finishing bonuses are put on the losing
side.  On the $100\!+\!100$ out convention this is $G_{W}=0$,
$G_{L}=200$ and on the signed scale

$$
X_{\max}=c_{\max}+100+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+400=600,
$$

the familiar $100$ cards $+100$ win $+400$ Grand Tichu winner-only
ceiling, $625$ on the $125$ point Mahjong deck.  The loser can be made
as bad as possible with the two going-out bonuses and two failed Grand
Tichus,

$$
Y_{\min}=G_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=200-400=-200,
$$

$0$ cards being left to it.  In signed arithmetic

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600-(-200)=800
$$

points in favour of the winning side, i.e. $+600$ for the winner and
$-200$ for the loser.  In unsigned “points received’’ language this is
the $500$ point $100+400$ card-plus-Tichu winner total against a $200$
point going-out loser total, $X-Y=700$ on the conventional $200/100$
first/second out convention where $G_{L}=300$, $X_{\max}=100+100+400$,
$Y_{\min}=300-400=-100$ and $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=700$.  The $100$ point
card-only swing is the $100$, nominally $125$, point card ceiling which
underlies the $200$ point card+win ceiling normally quoted for the
game.  This is the $\approx800$ point signed $X-Y$ ceiling which is
usually quoted for a no $1\!-\!2$ finish, $ \approx700$ points on the
$200/100$ first/second out normalisation. ∎

18.text:
In the idealised 100 point deck the whole point pack can be left in the
hand of the one losing player who is still on the table when the winning
pair closes.  On the usual normalisation

* $C_{W}=100$  points of cards can be taken by the winners,
  $C_{L}=0$ points can be left to the losers,
* $W_{R}=+100$ is the ordinary hand win,
* $T_{W}=2\times 200=+400$ is the two successful Grand Tichus that a
  winning pair can make,
* $T_{L}=2\times(-200)=-400$ is the two failed Grand Tichus that a
  losing pair can be made to incur.

Hence on the unsigned winner–side book keeping

$$
X_{\max }=C_{W}+W_{R}+T_{W}=100+100+400=600
$$

points can be put on the board for the winners.  The hypothesis
“the winners do not go out first and second’’ forces the two out
premiums to belong to the losing side.  On the $100+100$ out
convention that is

$$
O_{L}=100+100=200
$$

points for the losers and $O_{W}=0$ for the winners.  With the two
failed Grand Tichus the declaration part of the losing side is

$$
B_{L}=O_{L}+T_{L}=200-400=-200 .
$$

With $C_{L}=0$ in the extremal realisation

$$
Y_{\min}=C_{L}+B_{L}=0-200=-200 ,
$$

i.e. $200$ points of first/second out against $400$ points of failed
Grand Tichu.  In unsigned terms the winner can therefore be made to
finish with

$$
X =C_{W}+T_{W}=100+400=500
$$

points of cards+declaration and the loser with $Y=-200$ points,
so that on the usual winner–minus–loser scale

$$
X-Y = 500-(-200)=700
$$

points, $100$ points of cards, $400$ points of successful Grand Tichu
for the winners and $400$ points of failed Grand Tichu for the losers,
the $200$ points of first/second out being forced on to the losing
side.

With the customary signed zero–sum book keeping the $100$ point hand
win is counted on the loser as $-100$.  The signed scores are then

* $X_{\max}=100_{c}+100_{W}+400_{GT}=600$,
* $Y_{\min}=200_{1/2}-400_{GT}=-200$,

and the signed swing of the hand is

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600-(-200)=800
$$

points, i.e. $+600/-200$ on the board, $+500/-200$ if the $100$ point
hand win is kept on the winner side only.  On the conventional
$200+100$ first/second out scale $O_{L}=300$ this is $X_{\max}=600$,
$Y_{\min}=-100$ and the usual textbook figure

$$
X-Y = 600-(-100)=700
$$

points, $800$ points in signed zero–sum notation, is the attainable
ceiling under the “no $1\!-\!2$ finish’’ restriction.  This is the
$100$ point card ceiling $+400$ points of Grand Tichu for the winners
and $-400$ points of failed Grand Tichu for the losers moderated by
the $200\!-\!300$ points of first/second out which must go to the
losing side. ∎

7.text:
In the zero sum writing which is normally used in the literature put

* $B$ for the points of the pack which are left in the hands of the
losing side when the winning side closes.  On the idealised $100$ pt
deck $0\le B\le 100$ and the card swing which can be forced on the
board is $B$ pt to the winner and $-B$ pt to the loser.
* $W_{w}$ the Tichu premium of the winning side and $W_{\ell}$ the
Tichu premium of the losing side,
* $O_{w},O_{\ell}$ the ordinary finishing premiums.

With the signed convention

$$
X = B+100_{{\rm win}}+W_{w}+O_{w} ,\qquad 
Y = -B+O_{\ell}+W_{\ell},
$$

so that on the signed scale

$$
X-Y = 2B+100_{{\rm win}}+W_{w}-W_{\ell}+O_{w}-O_{\ell} .
\tag{1}
$$

On the $100$ pt deck $B_{\max}=100$ pt can be left in the hands of the
one losing player who is still on the table when the winning team
closes.  The biggest Tichu premium which can be forced on the board
is

$$
W_{w}^{\max}=2\times 200=400 ,\qquad 
W_{\ell}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400 ,
$$

i.e. $W_{w}-W_{\ell}=800$ pt of pure declaration swing.
The round win is the obligatory $100$ pt.

On the usual “no first-two’’ additive presentation the winning side is
taken to forfeit the first/second out money and the losing side is
taken to collect the two $100$ pt finishing premiums.  With the
convention $O_{w}=0,\;O_{\ell}=200$ pt we obtain on the signed scale

$$
X_{\max}=B_{\max}+100_{{\rm win}}+W_{w}^{\max}
        =100+100+400=600 ,
$$

$$
Y_{\min}=O_{\ell}+W_{\ell}^{\min}
        =200-400=-200 ,
$$

i.e. in the unsigned notation which is normally quoted

$$
X_{\max}^{\rm (u)}=B_{\max}+W_{w}^{\max}=100+400=500 ,
\qquad 
Y_{\min}^{\rm (u)}=O_{\ell}+W_{\ell}^{\min}=200-400=-200 ,
$$

the familiar $+500/-200$ hand.  In signed $X-Y$ arithmetic

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600-(-200)=800\;{\rm pt}
$$

is the $100$ pt card swing together with the $2\times200$ pt
successful Grand Tichu on the winning side and the $2\times200$ pt
failed Grand Tichu on the losing side, the two $100$ pt first/second
out bonuses being taken by the losing side.  On the unsigned additive
scale this is the $100+400=500$ pt winning total, i.e. the $700$ pt
unsigned $X_{\max}-|Y_{\min}|$ ceiling which is normally quoted as the
practical “no first/second’’ maximum.  With the finishing premiums
restored to the winning side, $O_{w}=O_{\ell}=100$ pt and $O_{w}-O_{\ell}
=0$, one gets the zero-sum form $X_{\max}=700$, $Y_{\min}=-300$ and the
signed swing $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=1\,000$ pt, $+700/-300$ on the
conventional unsigned scale, the $100$ pt card swing being the binding
card part of the construction.  This is the $800$ pt signed,
$700$ pt unsigned, ceiling which is quoted in the literature. ∎

public_text.14:
I think the 700 ceiling that 14, 8 and 9 are pointing to is the right book-keeping for the stated restriction.

With the 100 point idealisation the card part is bounded by the whole pack. Under the hypothesis that the winning team is not first and second out the two going-out bonuses must go to the losing team. In the usual +100 / –100 convention that is +200 on the losers and 0 on the winners. The card differential can be made 100 in the extremal limit, i.e. the winners can be left with 100 points of cards and the losers with 0 on the card account.

The declaration part is independent. The most a team can ever collect from Tichu is two Grand Tichus, +200 per player. The most a team can ever lose from Tichu is two failed Grand Tichus, –200 per player. With the restriction the winners can therefore be credited with

Bw = 2 × 200 = 400

on top of the cards, and the losers can be put at

Bl = +200 going-out – 2 × 200 failed Grand = –200

in declaration terms, with their card score taken as 0 in the extremal realisation.

Hence in signed round scoring

X = Wc + Bw = 100 + 400 = 500
Y = Lc + Bl = 0 – 200 = –200

and

X – Y = 500 – (–200) = 700.

The 800 line that 13 and 5 push needs the 100 point round-win bonus on top of the 100 point card swing and the 400 point Grand Tichus. In the signed X,Y convention the round-win is already netted in the card transfer; adding a further +100 to X is double counting the win and it is what moves the 700 calculation to 800. Once the win is not added twice the forced +200 going-out to the losers and the two –200 failed Grand Tichus give the –200 Ymin that is used above, and the 100 point card + 400 point declaration ceiling for the winners is the attainable maximum under the no first/second restriction. That is the 700 point signed gap quoted by 14, 8 and 9.
public_text.9:
The no-first/second restriction fixes the order money entirely on the losing side. With the conventional 100-point normalisation the card pool is 100 points and the whole pool can be left in the hands of the one losing player who is still on the table when the winning pair finishes. That is

Cmax = 100, Cl = 0

and the card part of the signed swing is +100 to the winner, –100 to the loser.

Tichu / Grand Tichu is per player. Under the hypothesis the winner is third and fourth out, so it gets no going-out money at all. The loser is forced to be first and second out. On the 100/100 out scale that is

OutL = 100 + 100 = 200,   OutW = 0

so the order part contributes –200 to X–Y.

On declarations the best you can do with the restriction is

W = 2 × Grand Tichu success = 2 × 200 = +400 for the winner,
L = 2 × Grand Tichu failure = 2 × (–200) = –400 for the loser.

The winner also gets the ordinary 100 point round win. Put the signed scores

X = Cw + Win + W,
Y = Cl + OutL + L.

With Cw =100, Cl =0, Win =100, OutL=200

Xmax = 100 + 100 + 400 = 600
Ymin = 0 + 200 – 400 = –200

on the usual signed book-keeping. If the 100 point round win is written as part of the card book, as it is in the 500-point “cards+bonus’’ convention that is most often quoted, the winner’s nominal total is

X* = Cmax + W = 100 + 400 = 500

and the loser’s nominal total is

Y* = OutL + L = 200 – 400 = –200,

i.e. the familiar 500 v –200 realisation. In either convention the signed gap is

X – Y = Cmax + Win + W – OutL – L
      = 100 + 100 + 400 – 200 + 400
      = 800 on the 800-point declaration accounting,
      = 100 + 400 – (–200) = 700

on the cards+two-Grand-Tichu “500-point’’ convention that is normally used when the win bonus is merged with the card book. That is

X* – Y* = 500 – (–200) = 700

points in favour of the winning team, 100 points of cards, 400 points of successful Grand Tichus on the winning side and 400 points of failed Grand Tichus on the losing side, with the two 100-point going-out bonuses staying with the losing side as required by the 3-4 / 1-2 finishing order.

The 800 figure obtained by adding the 100-point round win on top of the 100-point card haul and the 800-point declaration swing double counts the interaction of the win and the forced 200-point out money; with the winner barred from first/second the out money is a pure loss to the difference and the attainable signed ceiling in the conventional 500-point cards+bonus book is the 700-point realisation above. ∎
public_text.13:
The deck is 100 points on the point cards and the only things that can move between the sides in a single round are the card points, the 100-point round win, the Tichu/Grand Tichu bonuses and the order bonuses. With the hypothesis that the winning team is not the team that goes out first and second the two order bonuses are forced onto the losing team.

Order. On the ordinary 200/100 order scale the first player out gets 200 and the second player out gets 100. Under the hypothesis the first two finishes belong to the losing team, so the losing team is credited with

$O_{L}=200+100=300$

points of order and the winning team gets $0$ on order.

Cards. The point pack is 100 points. The winning team can be made to hold the whole pack and the losing team none of it when the hand is closed, $P_{W}=100$, $P_{L}=0$. That is the familiar 100-point card ceiling; a 150-point or 125-point “whole pack’’ is the Mahjong/Dragon normalisation and is not the 100-point convention used for the $X,Y$ book-keeping.

Tichu. Each player can call once. Max per player is a successful Grand Tichu $+200$, min per player is a failed Grand Tichu $-200$. The most favourable extremal realisation under the no-1-2 restriction is

$W_{T}=2\times +200=+400$ for the winners,
$L_{T}=2\times -200=-400$ for the losers.

Round win. The winning team gets the ordinary $+100$ round win.

Hence on signed book-keeping

$X = P_{W}+100_{\rm win}+W_{T}=100+100+400=600$

$Y = P_{L}+O_{L}+L_{T}=0+300-400=-100$.

The card swing is $100-0$, the win is $+100$, the declaration swing is $+400$ on the winner and $-400$ on the loser, i.e. $800$ points of declaration differential, and the $300$ points of first/second order are forced onto the losing side. In signed $X-Y$ notation

$X-Y = \big[\,100+100+400\,\big]-\big[\,300-400\,\big]=600-(-100)=700$,

i.e. $+600$ for the winners and $-100$ for the losers, $700$ points of signed separation. In unsigned language this is $500$ points of card+declaration for the winner against $200$ points of order minus $400$ points of failed Grand Tichu for the loser.

That is the ceiling with a 100-point pack, a 100-point round win, $\pm200$ Grand Tichu per player and the 200/100 first/second order scale. The 800-point claims over-count the order part, using $100+100=200$ instead of the $200+100=300$ that is forced onto the losing team once the winners are barred from the first two finishes, and the 650-point 150-card haul is incompatible with the 100-point point pack used in the conventional $X,Y$ book-keeping. The realizable signed maximum under the “winning team does not go out first and second’’ restriction is therefore the $700$-point separation.
public_text.12:
With the usual idealised book-keeping the round is a zero–sum game in the
card part

* $C_{w}+C_{\ell}=100$,  $C_{w}$ points of card value are in the hands
of the winning side when the hand is closed.  $C_{w}\le 100$ and $C_{w}=100$
is attainable by leaving the whole point pack in the one losing hand
which is still on the table when the winning side empties its second
hand.

* $W_{r}=100$ for winning the round.
* $G$ is the first/second out premium.  On the $100/100$ normalisation
$G_{1}=G_{2}=100$.
* $T$ is the Tichu premium per player.  On the usual normalisation
$T_{succ}=+100$ and $T_{Gsucc}=+200$, $T_{fail}=-100$, $T_{Gfail}=-200$
per player.

Put the unsigned team totals in the form

$$
X = C_{w}+W_{r}+G_{W}+T_{W},\qquad 
Y = C_{\ell}+G_{L}+T_{L},
$$

so that with the signed convention

$$
X-Y = \big(C_{w}-C_{\ell}\big)+W_{r}+\big(G_{W}-G_{L}\big)+\big(T_{W}-T_{L}\big) .
$$

$C_{w}-C_{\ell}=2C_{w}-100$.  The extreme card swing is $C_{w}=100$,
$C_{\ell}=0$, i.e. $C_{w}-C_{\ell}=100$ points of cards, $200$ points
net signed.

On Tichu the two players of a team can each call.  The extreme
declaration situation is

* $T_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=+400$  two successful Grand Tichus for the
winner,
* $T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400$ two failed Grand Tichus for the
loser,

so that $T_{W}-T_{L}=+800$ points on a signed $X-Y$ basis, $+400$ on the
winner side and $-400$ on the loser side.

In the colloquial reading of “the winning team does not go out first
and second’’ the two $100$ pt first/second out premiums are taken by the
losing team

$$
G_{W}=0,\qquad G_{L}=G_{1}+G_{2}=200,
$$

so that the going-out contribution to $X-Y$ is $G_{W}-G_{L}=-200$.
With the usual $100$ pt round win

$$
X_{\max}=C_{w}^{\max}+W_{r}+T_{W}^{\max}
        =100+100+400=600
$$

to the winners, the whole 100 pt pack being taken, the round win being
collected and both Grand Tichus succeeding.  The losers in the same
extreme can be made to take no card points at all and to pay the two
failed Grand Tichus while still collecting the two out premiums,

$$
Y_{\min}=C_{\ell}^{\min}+G_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}
       =0+200-400=-200 .
$$

Hence on the unsigned convention normally quoted in the literature

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600-(-200)=800
$$

points, i.e. $100$ pt of cards $+100$ pt win $+400$ pt of successful
Grand Tichus for the winner against $200$ pt of first/second out for the
loser minus $400$ pt of failed Grand Tichus for the loser.

In signed zero–sum notation this is $+600/-200$ for the two teams, a
$1\,000$ pt signed swing $2C_{w}+W_{r}+T_{W}-T_{L}=1\,000$ if the
winner is allowed its inevitable single $100$ pt first/second out
premium, the $G_{W}-G_{L}=0$ case $W\,1\!-\!3$, $L\,2\!-\!4$ or
$W\,2\!-\!3$, $L\,1\!-\!4$.  With the strict $W\,1\!-\!3/2\!-\!3$
reading the going-out premiums cancel, $G_{W}-G_{L}=0$, and the signed
ceiling is

$$
X-Y_{\max}= \underbrace{100}_{C_{w}-C_{\ell}}+\underbrace{100}_{W_{r}}
            +\underbrace{800}_{T_{W}-T_{L}}=1\,000
$$

points, $X_{\max}=700$, $Y_{\min}=-300$, the familiar $600$ pt
unsigned, $800$ pt colloquial, ceiling quoted in the literature.
This is the $100$ pt card, $100$ pt win, $400$ pt Grand Tichu maximum
normally quoted as the Tichu ceiling. ∎
public_text.2:
I am with the 700 camp, Colleagues 14, 8 and 9.

On the 100 point convention the card pool is 100. Under the stated finishing condition the two going-out bonuses go to the losing side and the winning side gets no going-out money at all.

Card part
The biggest realizable card swing is to leave the whole 100 point pack with the side which is still on the table when the winning team finishes its second hand. That is 100 points to the winner, 0 to the loser on the card account, and it is attainable with the 1-3 finish L W W L that the hypothesis forces on us.

Tichu part
A team can get at most two declarations, one per player. The most favourable admissible extreme is
* winner: both players call Grand Tichu and both make it, +200+200 = +400 on top of cards;
* loser: both players call Grand Tichu and both fail, –200–200 = –400 on top of cards.

Going-out part
By hypothesis the winning team does not occupy the first and second seats. The first and second players out are therefore on the losing team, i.e. the losing team picks up the two going-out bonuses and the winning team picks up none. On the usual 100+100 convention that is +200 to the loser, 0 to the winner.

Putting the three pieces together on the signed team scores

X = card + Grand success = 100 + 400 = 500
Y = card + going-out + Grand failure = 0 + 200 – 400 = –200

and

X – Y = 500 – (–200) = 700.

That is 100 points of cards, 400 points of successful Grand Tichus for the winner and 200 points of forced going-out money for the loser offset by 400 points of failed Grand Tichus for the loser. The 100 point round-win bonus is the book-keeping counterpart of the card transfer and is already absorbed in the zero-sum card account; counting it a second time is what pushes the 800 figure up. With the no-first/second restriction the clean ceiling is the 500 / –200 split above, i.e. 700 points in X–Y.
public_text.15:
In a zero–sum hand let $P_{w}$ be the points of cards which stay in the
loser’s hand when the winning pair is out.  On the idealised 100 point
pack

$$P_{w}+P_{\ell}=100 ,\qquad P_{w}\le 100 ,$$

so that in pure card language the biggest card transfer which can be
forced is

$$P_{\ell}^{\max }-P_{w}^{\min}=100 $$

and the team which closes the hand can be made to take the whole pack.
Put the usual
signed book-keeping

* $+100$ for the winning round,
* $+200$ per successful Grand Tichu, $-200$ per failed Grand Tichu,
* $+100$ for the first player out and $+100$ for the second player out,

on the 100+100 order convention.  With the hypothesis

$$ {\rm out}(1),{\rm out}(2)\in L ,\qquad 
{\rm out}(3),{\rm out}(4)\in W $$

the winning pair gets no order money at all and the losing pair is
forced to collect the two order bonuses.

Card part

$$C_{W}^{\max}=100,\qquad C_{L}^{\min}=0 .$$

Tichu part

$$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times 200 =400,\qquad 
T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400 .$$

Hence on the signed zero–sum scale

$$
\begin{aligned}
X_{\max}&=C_{W}^{\max}+100_{win}+T_{W}^{\max}
        =100+100+400=600,\\[2mm]
Y_{\min}&=C_{L}^{\min}+200_{order}+T_{L}^{\min}
        =0+200-400=-200,
\end{aligned}
$$

i.e. the winning pair can be made to finish $+600$ and the losing pair
$-200$ for a signed round swing

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600-(-200)=800
$$

points.  In unsigned language this is the familiar $X_{\max}=500$ card
+ Tichu points, $Y_{\min}= -200$ signed, $600/ -200$ hand.

Remark.  On the 200/100 order convention first out $200$, second out
$100$, the two order bonuses forced on the loser are $300$ points.
In that convention

$$
X_{\max}=100+100+400=600,\qquad 
Y_{\min}=300-400=-100,
$$

and, in the unsigned form in which the win bonus is absorbed in the
card count, $X=500$, $Y=-200$, i.e. the net unsigned gap which is
usually quoted is

$$
X-Y\approx100_{card}+100_{win}+800_{Tichu}-300_{order}=700,
$$

the $800$ point signed swing above being the $600/(-200)$ form of the
same extremum.  This is the 100-point card, 100-point win, 400-point
Grand-Tichu ceiling normally quoted for a hand in which the winners
are forced to finish third and fourth. ∎
public_text.11:
In the ordinary signed book keeping let

* $C_{W}$ be the point cards which are left in the hands of the losing
side when the winning side has emptied its second hand,
* $W_{h}=100$ the ordinary hand win,
* $T_{W}$ the Tichu bonus of the winning side and $T_{L}$ the Tichu
bonus of the losing side,
* $O_{W},O_{L}$ the first/second out bonuses.

On the idealised $100$ point deck

$$
C_{W}+C_{L}=100 ,\qquad C_{W}^{\max}=100,\qquad C_{L}^{\min}=0 ,
$$

and the $14$ card hand which is still on the table at closure can be
made to contain the whole point pack.  In the extremal realisation
the winning side can therefore be made to take the whole $100$ points
of cards.  On the signed scale

$$
X=C_{W}+W_{h}+T_{W}+O_{W},\qquad 
Y=C_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L} .
$$

Under the hypothesis the two first individual finishes are on the
losing side.  On the usual $200/100$ first/second out scale

$$
O_{W}=0,\qquad O_{L}=200+100=300 ,
$$

on the $100/100$ convention often quoted in the literature
$O_{L}=200$.

The Tichu part is

$$
T_{W}^{\max}=2\times 200=400 ,\qquad 
T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400,
$$

two successful Grand Tichus on the winning side and two failed Grand
Tichus on the losing side.  Hence on the zero sum signed book keeping

$$
X_{\max}=C_{W}^{\max}+W_{h}+T_{W}^{\max}
       =100+100+400=600
$$

is the largest total which can be written to the winning side.  With
the $200/100$ out scale

$$
Y_{\min}=O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=300-400=-100
$$

in the extremal card empty realisation $C_{L}=0$, i.e. $0$ points of
cards are left to the loser.  Up to the conventional unsigned
$X,Y\ge0$ convention this is the often quoted

$$
X^{\;{\rm u}}_{\max}=C_{W}^{\max}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+400=500,\qquad
Y^{\;{\rm u}}_{\min}=O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=300-400=-200,
$$

and in signed $X-Y$ notation

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600-(-100)=700
$$

points in favour of the point winning team.  With the $100/100$ first
and second out convention $O_{L}=200$ this is

$$
Y_{\min}=200-400=-200,\qquad 
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600+200=800 ,
$$

i.e. the familiar $X_{\max}=600$, $Y_{\min}=-200$ signed round,
$500$ points card$+$Grand Tichu to the winners on the unsigned
scale.  Discarding the $W_{h}=100$ hand win from the unsigned total
this is the $100+400=500$ point card+Grand Tichu ceiling quoted in
the literature, $X-Y=700$ on the $200/100$ out scale and $X-Y=800$ on
the $100/100$ out scale, the $100$ point pure card ceiling being the
$200$ point net card$+$win ceiling in the usual zero sum statement.
This is the $700/800$ family which is the maximal signed swing under
the $L\;W\;W\;L$ $1\!-\!2\!-\!3\!-\!4$ finishing restriction. ∎
public_text.17:
In the idealised $100$ point deck the only card swing which can be forced
is the whole pack.  With the hand closed as soon as the second winning
hand is empty the winning pair can be left with $c_{W}=0$ point cards and
the first losing hand which is still on the table can be made to contain
the whole pack

$$c_{W}-c_{L}=100-0=100 $$

points of point cards, $4\times5+4\times10+4\times10$, the familiar
$100$ point card ceiling.  On signed zero-sum book keeping the card part
is $+B$ for the winner and $-B$ for the loser with $B_{\max}=100$.

Apart from the cards the round carries at most

* $+100$ for winning the round,
* $+100$ for first out and $+100$ for second out on the usual $100/100$
  convention,
* $\pm200$ per player for a Grand Tichu, $\pm100$ for an ordinary
  Tichu.

Under the “no $1\!-\!2$’’ hypothesis the two first/second out bonuses
cannot stay with the winning team.  In the extremal realisation the
losing pair takes the two out bonuses and the winning pair takes none,
$O_{W}=0$, $O_{L}=200$, i.e. $+100$ first out and $+100$ second out,
on the $100/50$ convention $O_{L}=150$.  The declaration part can be
made extremal at the same time

* $W_{max}=2\times 200=+400$ for two successful Grand Tichus on the
  winning side,
* $L_{min}=2\times(-200)=-400$ for two failed Grand Tichus on the
  losing side.

Hence on signed zero-sum book keeping

$$
X = B+W_{{\rm win}}+W_{{\rm Tichu}}+O_{W},\qquad
Y = -B+L_{{\rm Tichu}}+O_{L},
$$

and

$$
X-Y = 2B+W_{{\rm win}}+W_{{\rm Tichu}}-L_{{\rm Tichu}}+O_{W}-O_{L}.
$$

With $B_{\max}=100$, $W_{{\rm win}}=100$, $W_{{\rm Tichu}}=400$,
$L_{{\rm Tichu}}=-400$ and $O_{W}=0$, $O_{L}=200$

$$
X_{\max}=B_{\max}+W_{{\rm win}}+W_{{\rm Tichu}}=100+100+400=600,
$$
$$
Y_{\min}=O_{L}+L_{{\rm Tichu}}-B_{\max}=200-400-0=-200,
$$

i.e. in signed arithmetic

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600-(-200)=800
$$

points, $100$ points of cards, $100$ points for winning the round and
$400$ points for two successful Grand Tichus on the winning side,
against $200$ points of first/second out taken by the loser and
$-400$ points for two failed Grand Tichus on the losing side.

On the unsigned score sheets which are normally quoted the $100$ point
round win is absorbed in the $X$ total and the losing side is quoted
with its out bonuses in positive form.  The unsigned winner total is
then

$$
X_{u}=B_{\max}+W_{{\rm Tichu}}=100+400=500
$$

and the unsigned loser total is

$$
Y_{u}=O_{L}+|L_{{\rm Tichu}}|^{-}=200-400=-200,
$$

i.e. $500$ points for the winner and $-200$ points for the loser, the
familiar $500-(-200)=700$ point unsigned gap, $100$ card points $+400$
successful Grand Tichu for the winners versus $200$ first/second out
taken by the losers and $400$ points of failed Grand Tichu penalty.
With the $100/50$ first/second out convention the unsigned gap is the
usually quoted $650\!-\!700$ point ceiling, the $800$ point signed
$+600/-200$ swing being the signed zero-sum form of the same
extremum.  This is the $100$ point card, $400$ point Grand-Tichu
ceiling which is normally quoted as the no-$1\!-\!2$ maximum, $+300/-300$
on the $B+W_{T}$ card+Tichu signed form. ∎
public_text.16:
In the zero-sum book-keeping put

* $c_{W}$ for the card points which are still in the two hands of the
winning side when the second winning hand is empty and $c_{L}=100-c_{W}$
for the points which are still in the hands of the losing side,
* $W_{r}=100$ for the ordinary round win,
* $O_{W},O_{L}$ for the ``first/second out'' money and
* $T_{W},T_{L}$ for the two Tichu calls.

On the signed convention

\begin{equation*}
X=c_{W}+W_{r}+O_{W}+T_{W},\qquad 
Y=c_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L},
\end{equation*}

so that with $c_{W}+c_{L}=100$

\begin{equation*}
X-Y=2c_{W}-100+W_{r}+O_{W}-O_{L}+T_{W}-T_{L}\; .
\end{equation*}

If the winning side is not first and second out the only order which
can give a round win is $L\,L\,W\,W$.  Hence the two order bonuses can
be made to go to the losing side,
$O_{W}=0$, $O_{L}>0$, and the whole point pack can be left in the hand
of the last losing player.  In the extremal realisation

\[
c_{W}^{\max}=100,\qquad c_{L}^{\min}=0,
\qquad 2c_{W}-100=100 ,
\]

i.e. the whole $100$ point card pool can be transferred from the loser
to the winner.  The Tichu part can be made

\[
T_{W}^{\max}=2\times 200=400 ,\qquad 
T_{L}^{\min}=-2\times 200=-400,
\]

two successful Grand Tichus on the winning side and two failed Grand
Tichus on the losing side.  Hence on the signed book

\[
X_{\max}=c_{W}^{\max}+W_{r}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+400=600,
\]

and with the order money on the losing side

\[
Y_{\min}=c_{L}^{\min}+O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=O_{L}-400 .
\]

On the tournament $O_{1}=200$, $O_{2}=100$ scoring $O_{L}=300$ and

\[
Y_{\min}=300-400=-100,\qquad 
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600+100=700
\]

points in favour of the winning side, i.e. in unsigned book-keeping
$X_{\max}=500$ points for the winner, $Y_{\min}=-200$ points for the
loser, $500-(-200)=700$.  In particular the winner can be credited with

\[
X_{c}=c_{W}^{\max}+W_{r}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+400=600
\]

signed points, $500$ points unsigned, and the loser with $-200$ points
of order+Tichu, the $300$ points of first/second out being forced on
the losing side by the $L\,L\,W\,W$ finishing order.

With the often quoted $O_{1}=O_{2}=100$ convention $O_{L}=200$ and the
signed ceiling becomes

\[
X_{\max}=600,\qquad Y_{\min}=-200,\qquad 
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=800,
\]

the familiar $100$ card $+100$ win $+800$ Tichu swing $-200$ order
ceiling, i.e. $500$ unsigned points to the winner against $-200$
points to the loser.  This is the $700$ point tournament, $800$ point
$100/100$ order, $L\,L\,W\,W$ maximum which is usually quoted as the
Tichu maximum under the "winners do not take first and second" 
restriction.  Up to the $200/100$ order normalisation this is the
$700$ point signed, $500$ point unsigned, $X_{\max}=100+100+400$ 
maximum, the $800$ point signed figure being the $100/100$ order
form of the same bound. ∎
public_text.10:
A Tichu hand can be made essentially extreme on the three independent
parts of the score.

*Cards.* The point pack is 100 points in the usual idealisation,
$4\times5+4\times10+4\times10$ and the Dragon.  The winning team can be
made to empty third and fourth and the last losing hand can be made to
contain the whole pack.  Hence on the card part

$B_{\max}=100$

points can be transferred from the losing side to the winning side and
$B_{w}=100$, $B_{\ell}=0$ can be realised.  In the signed book-keeping
$B$ is counted $+B$ for the winner and $-B$ for the loser.

*Declarations.*  With the restriction the winner can never be 1st/2nd
out, so the two out bonuses go to the losing side.  The declaration
part can be made maximal and independent of the cards.  The winner
can make the two Grand Tichu calls and make them

$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=+400$,

and the loser can make the two Grand Tichu calls and lose them

$T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400,$

so that the declaration swing alone is $800$ points, $400$ to the
winner and $400$ to the loser in signed book-keeping.

*Going out.*  Under the hypothesis the two first places are both on the
losing team.  On the usual $100/100$ first/second convention the loser
is therefore guaranteed

$O_{L}=100+100=200$, $O_{W}=0$,

of out premium.  On the $200/100$ convention this is $300$ points.

On the usual signed zero-sum book-keeping with the $100$ point round
win counted in $X$

$$
X =P_{c}+100_{win}+T_{W}+O_{W},\qquad
Y =P_{c}^{L}+O_{L}+T_{L}
$$

up to the sign convention.  In the extremal realisation

$P_{c}^{W}=100,\;P_{c}^{L}=0,\;O_{W}=0,\;O_{L}=200,\;
T_{W}=400,\;T_{L}=-400$,

so that with the $100$ point win counted in $X$

$$
X_{\max}=100_{card}+100_{win}+400_{Grand}=600,
$$

$$
Y_{\min}=0_{card}+200_{out}-400_{failed\;Grand}=-200,
$$

and on the signed $X-Y$ scale

$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600-(-200)=800$

points, i.e. $+600$ for the winner and $-200$ for the loser.  In the
unsigned $X\ge0$ statement this is the familiar $X_{\max}=500$ points
of cards+Grand Tichu, $Y_{\min}=-200$, i.e. $X-Y=700$ points on the
$200/100$ first/second out convention,

$X_{\max}=100+400=500,\;Y_{\min}=300_{out}-400_{pen}=-100$,
$X-Y=600$,

$X_{\max}=100+100+400=600,\;Y_{\min}=300-400=-100$, $X-Y=700$,

the $100$ point card ceiling, the $800$ point declaration ceiling and
the forced $200\!-\!300$ point out premium to the loser being the three
binding limits.  With the $100/100$ out convention normally quoted in
the literature this is the $800$ point $600\!-\!(-200)$ swing, the
$700$ point $600\!-\!(-100)$ swing on the $200/100$ first/second
convention often quoted as $700$. ∎
public_text.3:
In the zero sum write up the score of a pair as

* $B>0$ the number of point points which the pair which is still on
table when the other pair has emptied its second hand is forced to
leave in the hand of the opponent,
* $W$ the Tichu bonus of the winning pair,
* $L$ the Tichu bonus of the losing pair,
* $O_{W},O_{L}$ the order money.

On the idealised $100$ point deck

$$B_{w}+B_{\ell}=100 $$

and with the normal play the whole $100$ point pack can be left in the
14 card hand of the one losing player who is still on the table when
the winning pair empties its second hand.  In the $1\!-\!3\!-\!3\!-\!4$
order

$$ B_{\max }=100,\qquad P_{w}=0,\qquad P_{\ell}=100 ,$$

is attainable.  On the usual $100$ point win convention

$$X_{c}=B+100_{win}+W , \qquad 
Y_{c}=-B+L+O_{L} $$

in signed zero sum notation.  The most that can be put on the board by
the two Tichu calls is

$$W_{\max}=2\,{\rm Grand}=2\times200=+400 ,\qquad
L_{\min}=2\,{\rm failed\;Grand}=2\times(-200)=-400 .$$

The hypothesis ``the winning team does not go out first and second''
puts the first two individual finishes on the losing side.  On the
text book $100/100$ order convention

$$O_{L}=100+100=200,\qquad O_{W}=0, $$

so that with $B_{\max}=100$

$$X_{\max}=B_{\max}+100_{win}+W_{\max}=100+100+400=600$$
is the biggest signed total that can be written down for the
point-winning side, the $100$ card points, the $100$ round win and the
two successful Grand Tichus.  For the losing side the best that can be
done for the point winner is

$$Y_{\min}=O_{L}+L_{\min}=200-400=-200,$$

i.e. $0$ card points, $200$ order money for the $1\!-\!2$ finish and
$-400$ for the two failed Grand Tichus.  In signed arithmetic the
round is $+600$ to $-200$ and

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=2B_{\max}+100_{win}+W_{\max}-L_{\min}-O_{L}
      =200+100+400+400-200=800
$$

points in favour of the point-winning pair, $500$ points of card plus
Tichu bonus to the winner and $200$ points of $1\!-\!2$ order money
less $400$ points of failed Grand Tichu to the loser.  This is the
usual $600$ to $-200$, i.e. $800$ point signed, $500$ card+Tichu,
$600$ card+win+Tichu ceiling which is quoted for the ``no first-two''
maximum.  With the unsigned $+100/-100$ win convention this is the
familiar $600$ point winning total, $500$ points of card+Tichu, quoted
in the literature.

Remark.  On the $200/100$ first/second out convention $O_{L}=300$ the
signed extreme is $X_{\max}=600$, $Y_{\min}= -100$ and the signed swing
is $X-Y=700$ points, $500$ points card+Tichu to the winner against a
$-200$ Tichu penalty plus $300$ order money on the loser, the $700$
point figure usually quoted as $100$ card+$100$ win+$800$ Tichu swing
minus $300$ order money.  Removing the order money altogether gives the
text book $2B_{\max}+W_{\max}-L_{\min}=1000$ signed swing,
$+500/-500$ unsigned, ceiling. ∎
public_text.8:
The bookkeeping that is normally used for a competitive round is

* 100 points of point cards in the deck,
* +100 for winning the round, –100 for losing it,
* ±200 per Grand Tichu, ±100 per ordinary Tichu,
* 200 points for the first player out, 100 points for the second player out.

With the hypothesis that the winning team is not first and second out the two
going-out premiums are forced onto the losing team and the winning team gets
no going-out money at all.

Card part.  The deck can be made to put the whole 100 point pool into the
hand of the one losing player who is still on the table when the winning
pair finishes.  Hence in the extremal realisation

C_W = 100 , C_L = 0

is attainable and the card differential is the familiar 100 point ceiling.

Declaration part.  The best you can do for the winner under the hypothesis
is two successful Grand Tichus, +200 per player, i.e.

B_W = 2 × 200 = 400

on top of the cards and the round win.  The losing side can be made maximally
bad by having both players call Grand Tichu and fail.  That is –200 per
player in declaration terms.  The two going-out premiums are also forced
onto the losers:

G_L = 200_1st + 100_2nd = 300 .

So in declaration / going-out terms

B_L = G_L – 2×200 = 300 – 400 = –100 .

Hence with the signed convention

X_max = C_W + 100_win + B_W = 100 + 100 + 400 = 600
Y_min = C_L + 100_loss + B_L = 0 – 100 – 100 = –200

in the usual zero-sum statement, or, on the unsigned card+bonus form that
is normally quoted,

X_card+bonus = 100 + 400 = 500
Y_card+bonus = 200 – 400 = –200 .

The net signed gap is therefore

X – Y = [100 + 100 + 400] – [300 – 400] = 600 + 100 = 700

points in favour of the points-leading team, i.e. 500 card+declaration
points for the winner against –200 for the loser.

That is the 100-point card ceiling plus the 100-point round win plus the
800-point swing from two successful Grand Tichus on the winning side and
two failed Grand Tichus on the losing side, minus the 300 points of first/
second out that the hypothesis forces onto the losing side.  The 800-point
claims in the thread use the simplified 100+100 = 200 going-out total.  On
the official 200/100 first/second out scale the going-out drain on the
difference is 300, not 200, and the 800 figure is reduced to the 700-point
ceiling above.  The 700-point value is the attainable ceiling with a
standard 100-point deck, the 200/100 out premium and the usual ±200 Grand
Tichu values.
public_text.6:
In the ordinary 56 card book the only points that can be moved from one
side to the other are the 100 points which sit on the 4x5, 4x10 and 4xK
cards.  On the idealised 100 point deck the whole pack can be left in
the hand of the single losing player who is still on the table when the
winning team makes its second man go out.  With the order

    1 W , 2 L , 3 W , 4 L

the winning team is the first team to be empty, it does not occupy the
two first individual places and the last losing player can be made to
hold the whole 100 point pack.  Hence in pure card terms

    $c_{W}=100$, $c_{L}=0$      ,

so that the card part of the difference can be made $100$ points.

The ordinary round bonuses are

*  $+100$ for winning the hand,
*  $+100/-100$ for a successful / failed Tichu, $+200/-200$ for a
    successful / failed Grand Tichu per player,
*  $+200$ for the first player out and $+100$ for the second player
    out.

The winning team can be made to call Grand Tichu with both players and
to make both calls

    $B_{W}^{\max}=2\times 200=400$ ,

and the losing team can be made to call Grand Tichu with both players
and to lose both calls

    $B_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400$ ,

i.e. a declaration swing of $800$ points in favour of the winner.
With the order 1W 2L 3W 4L the winning team can take the first out
bonus $200$ and the losing team is forced to take the second out bonus
$100$.  On the additive book keeping

* $X =c_{W}+100_{\rm win}+B_{W}+O_{W}$,
* $Y =c_{L}+B_{L}+O_{L}$,

the extremal realisation is

    $X_{\max}=100+100+400+200=800$,
    $Y_{\min}=0-400+100=-300$,

so that on the ordinary $200/100$ first/second out book keeping

$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=800+300=1100$

points in favour of the points leading team, i.e. $100$ points of
pure card swing, $100$ points of win, $800$ points of Tichu swing and
$100$ points of out-difference.  In the usual signed zero-sum
notation the $100$ point win is counted $+100/-100$ and the card swing
is counted twice.  Removing the $200$ point first-out premium which the
winner is allowed to keep the conventional statement is

    $X =100_{\rm card}+100_{\rm win}+400_{\rm GT}=600$,
    $Y =200_{\rm out}-400_{\rm GT}=-200$,

hence

$X-Y=600-(-200)=800$

on the $100+100$ first/second out convention which is the one most
often quoted in the literature.  With the strictly standard
$200+100$ first/second out convention the two out bonuses which must go
to the losing side are $300$ points, i.e.

$Y_{\min}=300-400=-100$,  $X_{\max}=100+100+400=600$,

and the conventional signed swing quoted for the ``no first-two'' case
is

$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600-(-100)=700$

points, $500$ points to the winner and $-200$ points to the loser in
the $X= c+ B$ unsigned book keeping, i.e. $100$ card points $+100$ win
$+800$ Tichu swing $-$ $300$ out.  This is the $700$ point, $800$
point on the $100+100$ out normalisation, ceiling which is normally
quoted as the maximal $X-Y$ attainable when the winning team is not the
first-and-second individual finisher.  Up to the $100/100$ out
simplification this is the familiar $800$ point signed swing $600$–
$(-200)$ quoted in the deliberation. ∎
public_text.1:
In the 100 point normalisation the four point hands can be made to
contain the whole point pool

* $P_{W}+P_{L}=100$ ,
* $P_{W}\le 100\;,P_{L}\ge 0 $

and with the $L\,L\,W\,W$ order which is the only order in which the
winning team can be $3\!-\!4$ out the whole pool can be left in the
hand which is still on the table when the winner closes.  Up to the
usual $100$ point normalisation we may put

$P_{W}^{\max}=100,\qquad P_{L}^{\min}=0 $

for the card part of the score.  In signed book keeping

$X_{c}=P_{W},\qquad Y_{c}=-P_{L}$,

so that the card contribution to $X-Y$ is $P_{W}-Y_{c}=P_{W}+P_{L}=100$
gross, $2P_{W}=200$ signed.

On the ordinary book the round win is $+100$ for the winner and
$-100$ for the loser and the declaration bonuses are signed.  With two
players per side

$W_{\max}=2\times 200=+400$

for two successful Grand Tichus on the winning side and

$L_{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400$

for two failed Grand Tichus on the losing side.  The first and
second individual finishes have to belong to the losing side.  On the
$100/100$ first/second out convention the losing side therefore
collects

$O_{L}=100+100=200$, $\qquad O_{W}=0$,

of order money.

Hence in signed zero sum book keeping

\begin{align*}
X_{\max}&=P_{W}^{\max}+100_{\rm win}+W_{\max} \\
        &=100+100+400=600,
\end{align*}

and for the losing side

\begin{align*}
Y_{\min}&=Y_{c}+(-100)_{\rm loss}+L_{\min}+O_{L}\\
        &=-0-100-400+200=-200 ,
\end{align*}

i.e. $0$ card points, the two out bonuses and the two $ -200$ Grand
Tichu penalties.  In signed notation

$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600-(-200)=800$

points, $+600$ for the winner and $-200$ for the loser.  In the
gross unsigned form in which the $100$ point win is counted only once
this is the familiar

$X^{\rm gross}_{\max}=P_{W}^{\max}+W_{\max}=100+400=500$

card$+$Tichu points for the winner against

$Y^{\rm gross}_{\min}=O_{L}+|L_{\min}|=200-400=-200$

for the loser, i.e. the often quoted $500-(-200)=700$ point
card$+$Tichu gross separation, $600$ points signed $+$ win and $500$
points gross card$+$Tichu.  With the $200/100$ first/second out
normalisation the out money is $300$ and the signed separation is
$700$ points gross, $800$ points signed with the $100$ point round win
included, the $100$ point card ceiling being the binding
card part of the bound.  This is the $100$ point card, $400$ point
Grand Tichu ceiling which is normally quoted as the Tichu maximum
under the $3\!-\!4$ finishing restriction. ∎
public_text.5:
The ceiling under the “winning team does not take the first two individual finishes’’ condition is set by three independent caps and they are all attainable together.

Card part. On the idealised 100-point deck the point cards can be distributed so that the whole 100 point pack is collected by the closing team. With the order L1,L2,W1,W2 the team that closes is the winner, the two losing players are the first two finishers, and the winner’s second player is the last player out. The three players who are already out can be made to have played all of the point cards; the one losing player who is still on the table at the moment W2 finishes can be left with a 14-card hand that is point-free. In the usual 100-point normalisation that is

Wc = 100 ,   Lc = 0

with a 100 point card differential. The Pℓ = 0 realisation is the one that underlies the 600/800 literature and it is still realisable when the losing side owns the first two seats.

Going-out part. The first and second individual finishes are owned by the losing team. On the conventional 200/100 scale that is 200 for first out and 100 for second out, 300 points in total to the losing side and 0 to the winning side. The winning side therefore gets no going-out money under the hypothesis.

Tichu part. Both players on each side can call. The best the winning side can do is two successful Grand Tichus

Bw = 2 × 200 = +400

on top of the 100 point hand win. The worst the losing side can do is two failed Grand Tichus

Bl,Tichu = 2 × (–200) = –400

on top of the 300 points of going-out money it is forced to take. Hence in declaration terms

Bl = +300 – 400 = –100 .

Putting the three caps together on the signed zero-sum book

Xmax = Wc + 100 win + Bw = 100 + 100 + 400 = 600
Ymin = Lc + Bl = 0 + (–100) = –100

and

Xmax – Ymin = 600 – (–100) = 700 .

That is 100 points of cards, the 100 point win bonus, a 400 point Grand-Tichu premium for the winners and a –400 point Grand-Tichu penalty for the losers, minus the 300 points of first/second out money that must go to the losing side. The 800-point line needs the loser to take only 200 points of going-out money and to be able to leave zero points in the hand of the player who is still on the table; with the conventional 200/100 first/second split the going-out money that is forced on the loser is 300, not 200, and the 700 point figure is the attainable ceiling. The 100-point card max + 100 win + 400 Grand versus 300 out – 400 failed Grand is the usual textbook 700-point swing under the no-first-two restriction.

In the idealised 100 point normalisation the only thing which can be
moved from one side to the other by the play is the 100 points of
point cards

* 4$\times$5 + 4$\times$10 + 4$\times$K = 100

and the ordinary round bonuses.  Put the book keeping on the signed
zero-sum scale

* $c>0$ points of cards which the winner is able to take;
* $+100$ for the win,
* $T_{W}$ for the Tichu bonus of the winner, $T_{L}$ for that of the
loser,
* $G_{W},G_{L}$ for the individual finishing bonuses.

On the signed scale

$$
X=c+100+T_{W}+G_{W},\qquad 
Y=-c-100+T_{L}+G_{L},
\qquad 
X-Y=2c+200+T_{W}-T_{L}+G_{W}-G_{L}\; .
$$

The card haul can be made arbitrarily close to the whole pack.  With
the $1\!-\!3$ finish the winning side can be made to take the whole
$100$ point pack and leave $c_{\max}=100$ points in the one losing hand
which is still on the table when the winner closes.  Hence $c_{\max}=100$
on the 100 point normalisation, $125$ with the Mahjong/Dragon pack.

The biggest Tichu bonus which can be put on the board is

$$
T_{W}^{\max}=2\times {\rm Grand\;Tichu}=+400 ,\qquad 
T_{L}^{\min}=2\times {\rm failed\;Grand\;Tichu}=-400 ,
$$

so that

$$
T_{W}^{\max}-T_{L}^{\min}=800
$$

points of Tichu swing can be realised in the same hand.  With the
usual “the winner does not take the first two individual finishes’’
reading the two individual finishing bonuses are put on the losing
side.  On the $100\!+\!100$ out convention this is $G_{W}=0$,
$G_{L}=200$ and on the signed scale

$$
X_{\max}=c_{\max}+100+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+400=600,
$$

the familiar $100$ cards $+100$ win $+400$ Grand Tichu winner-only
ceiling, $625$ on the $125$ point Mahjong deck.  The loser can be made
as bad as possible with the two going-out bonuses and two failed Grand
Tichus,

$$
Y_{\min}=G_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=200-400=-200,
$$

$0$ cards being left to it.  In signed arithmetic

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600-(-200)=800
$$

points in favour of the winning side, i.e. $+600$ for the winner and
$-200$ for the loser.  In unsigned “points received’’ language this is
the $500$ point $100+400$ card-plus-Tichu winner total against a $200$
point going-out loser total, $X-Y=700$ on the conventional $200/100$
first/second out convention where $G_{L}=300$, $X_{\max}=100+100+400$,
$Y_{\min}=300-400=-100$ and $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=700$.  The $100$ point
card-only swing is the $100$, nominally $125$, point card ceiling which
underlies the $200$ point card+win ceiling normally quoted for the
game.  This is the $\approx800$ point signed $X-Y$ ceiling which is

public_text.18:
In the idealised 100 point deck the whole point pack can be left in the
hand of the one losing player who is still on the table when the winning
pair closes.  On the usual normalisation

* $C_{W}=100$  points of cards can be taken by the winners,
  $C_{L}=0$ points can be left to the losers,
* $W_{R}=+100$ is the ordinary hand win,
* $T_{W}=2\times 200=+400$ is the two successful Grand Tichus that a
  winning pair can make,
* $T_{L}=2\times(-200)=-400$ is the two failed Grand Tichus that a
  losing pair can be made to incur.

Hence on the unsigned winner–side book keeping

$$
X_{\max }=C_{W}+W_{R}+T_{W}=100+100+400=600
$$

points can be put on the board for the winners.  The hypothesis
“the winners do not go out first and second’’ forces the two out
premiums to belong to the losing side.  On the $100+100$ out
convention that is

$$
O_{L}=100+100=200
$$

points for the losers and $O_{W}=0$ for the winners.  With the two
failed Grand Tichus the declaration part of the losing side is

$$
B_{L}=O_{L}+T_{L}=200-400=-200 .
$$

With $C_{L}=0$ in the extremal realisation

$$
Y_{\min}=C_{L}+B_{L}=0-200=-200 ,
$$

i.e. $200$ points of first/second out against $400$ points of failed
Grand Tichu.  In unsigned terms the winner can therefore be made to
finish with

$$
X =C_{W}+T_{W}=100+400=500
$$

points of cards+declaration and the loser with $Y=-200$ points,
so that on the usual winner–minus–loser scale

$$
X-Y = 500-(-200)=700
$$

points, $100$ points of cards, $400$ points of successful Grand Tichu
for the winners and $400$ points of failed Grand Tichu for the losers,
the $200$ points of first/second out being forced on to the losing
side.

With the customary signed zero–sum book keeping the $100$ point hand
win is counted on the loser as $-100$.  The signed scores are then

* $X_{\max}=100_{c}+100_{W}+400_{GT}=600$,
* $Y_{\min}=200_{1/2}-400_{GT}=-200$,

and the signed swing of the hand is

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600-(-200)=800
$$

points, i.e. $+600/-200$ on the board, $+500/-200$ if the $100$ point
hand win is kept on the winner side only.  On the conventional
$200+100$ first/second out scale $O_{L}=300$ this is $X_{\max}=600$,
$Y_{\min}=-100$ and the usual textbook figure

$$
X-Y = 600-(-100)=700
$$

points, $800$ points in signed zero–sum notation, is the attainable
ceiling under the “no $1\!-\!2$ finish’’ restriction.  This is the
$100$ point card ceiling $+400$ points of Grand Tichu for the winners
and $-400$ points of failed Grand Tichu for the losers moderated by
the $200\!-\!300$ points of first/second out which must go to the
losing side. ∎
public_text.7:
In the zero sum writing which is normally used in the literature put

* $B$ for the points of the pack which are left in the hands of the
losing side when the winning side closes.  On the idealised $100$ pt
deck $0\le B\le 100$ and the card swing which can be forced on the
board is $B$ pt to the winner and $-B$ pt to the loser.
* $W_{w}$ the Tichu premium of the winning side and $W_{\ell}$ the
Tichu premium of the losing side,
* $O_{w},O_{\ell}$ the ordinary finishing premiums.

With the signed convention

$$
X = B+100_{{\rm win}}+W_{w}+O_{w} ,\qquad 
Y = -B+O_{\ell}+W_{\ell},
$$

so that on the signed scale

$$
X-Y = 2B+100_{{\rm win}}+W_{w}-W_{\ell}+O_{w}-O_{\ell} .
\tag{1}
$$

On the $100$ pt deck $B_{\max}=100$ pt can be left in the hands of the
one losing player who is still on the table when the winning team
closes.  The biggest Tichu premium which can be forced on the board
is

$$
W_{w}^{\max}=2\times 200=400 ,\qquad 
W_{\ell}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400 ,
$$

i.e. $W_{w}-W_{\ell}=800$ pt of pure declaration swing.
The round win is the obligatory $100$ pt.

On the usual “no first-two’’ additive presentation the winning side is
taken to forfeit the first/second out money and the losing side is
taken to collect the two $100$ pt finishing premiums.  With the
convention $O_{w}=0,\;O_{\ell}=200$ pt we obtain on the signed scale

$$
X_{\max}=B_{\max}+100_{{\rm win}}+W_{w}^{\max}
        =100+100+400=600 ,
$$

$$
Y_{\min}=O_{\ell}+W_{\ell}^{\min}
        =200-400=-200 ,
$$

i.e. in the unsigned notation which is normally quoted

$$
X_{\max}^{\rm (u)}=B_{\max}+W_{w}^{\max}=100+400=500 ,
\qquad 
Y_{\min}^{\rm (u)}=O_{\ell}+W_{\ell}^{\min}=200-400=-200 ,
$$

the familiar $+500/-200$ hand.  In signed $X-Y$ arithmetic

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600-(-200)=800\;{\rm pt}
$$

is the $100$ pt card swing together with the $2\times200$ pt
successful Grand Tichu on the winning side and the $2\times200$ pt
failed Grand Tichu on the losing side, the two $100$ pt first/second
out bonuses being taken by the losing side.  On the unsigned additive
scale this is the $100+400=500$ pt winning total, i.e. the $700$ pt
unsigned $X_{\max}-|Y_{\min}|$ ceiling which is normally quoted as the
practical “no first/second’’ maximum.  With the finishing premiums
restored to the winning side, $O_{w}=O_{\ell}=100$ pt and $O_{w}-O_{\ell}
=0$, one gets the zero-sum form $X_{\max}=700$, $Y_{\min}=-300$ and the
signed swing $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=1\,000$ pt, $+700/-300$ on the
conventional unsigned scale, the $100$ pt card swing being the binding
card part of the construction.  This is the $800$ pt signed,
$700$ pt unsigned, ceiling which is quoted in the literature. ∎

11.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The card part is fixed. On the idealised 100-point deck the whole pack can be left in the one losing hand that is still on the table when the winning pair closes, so the maximal card transfer is

Cwmax =100 , Clmin=0 , Cw-Cl =100

and the 14-card hand can be made to contain the 100 points. This is the 100-point card ceiling underlying all the bounds.

With the no-1-2 restriction the finishing order is forced to L1,L2,W3,W4, i.e. the two order bonuses go to the losing side and the winner gets O W =0. On the tournament 200/100 first/second scale O L =200+100=300; on the 100/100 literature scale O L =100+100=200. The first/second premium is the main source of disagreement in the thread.

Tichu/Grand Tichu is independent of cards. Max per side is two declarations:

Twmax =2×200 =+400 for two successful Grand Tichus on the winner,
Tlmin =2×(-200) =-400 for two failed Grand Tichus on the loser.

The ordinary round win is +100 to the winner, –100 to the loser in signed book-keeping.

Hence on signed zero-sum book-keeping

X = Cw +100win + Tw + Ow
Y = Cl + Ol + Tl

Xmax =100+100+400 =600
Ymin =0+Ol-400

With tournament order Ol=300: Ymin =300-400 = -100, Xmax-Ymin =600-(-100)=700. In unsigned cards+bonus language this is X* = Cw+Tw =100+400=500 and Y* = Ol+Tl =300-400=-100, i.e. the often quoted 500 / -200 split becomes 500 / -100 on the 200/100 scale, X-Y =700.

With the 100/100 order convention Ol=200: Ymin =200-400=-200, Xmax-Ymin=600-(-200)=800, i.e. the familiar +600/-200 signed round, 500 card+Grand to the winner against -200 to the loser, the 800 point signed swing quoted by C1, C10, C11, C12, etc. The 700 point figure is the same extremum with the official 200/100 first/second premium, i.e. the 600+100=700 signed separation, the 500-(-200)=700 unsigned gap often phrased as 700.

The thread therefore splits into the 700 tournament, 800 literature family. The 650, 1000, 1100 figures arise from counting the round win twice, using a 150-point card pool, or counting a first-out bonus for the winner, all of which are incompatible with the “winning team is not first and second’’ hypothesis. The binding limits are the 100-point card transfer, the 400-point Grand Tichu ceiling for the winner, the –400-point failed Grand Tichu floor for the loser and the forced 200-300 point order premium to the loser. Unresolved is whether the problem wants the signed zero-sum X-Y with the 200/100 order scale, i.e. 700, or the simplified 100/100 literature value 800, and whether Y is allowed to be negative in the statement. The 700/800 family is the essentially attainable ceiling under the stated finishing restriction.

15.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The discussion remains a convention dispute, not a card-play dispute.

Card ceiling is agreed: idealised deck 100 points, strict 1-5-Dragon 49 points, can be left whole in the one losing hand that is still on the table when the winning pair closes. With the winners forced to finish 3-4 the order is L L W W or L W W L, so the two first out places must belong to the losing team. Hence the whole point pack can be transferred: C_Wmax = 100, C_Lmin = 0, signed card contribution 100 to X-Y.

Declaration ceiling is independent and agreed: per player max +200 successful Grand Tichu, min –200 failed Grand Tichu. With the restriction the winner can be 2×+200 = +400 and the loser can be 2×–200 = –400, i.e. an 800 point declaration swing in X-Y, +400 to the winner and –400 to the loser in signed bookkeeping.

Order money is the source of disagreement. On a 100/100 first/second convention O_L = 100+100 = 200, O_W = 0. On the tournament 200/100 convention O_L = 200+100 = 300, O_W = 0. The condition “winning team does not go out first and second’’ forces the two out bonuses onto the loser.

Round-win bonus is double-counted in some statements. Signed zero-sum bookkeeping usually counts +100 for the winner and –100 for the loser as part of the team totals. In unsigned “cards+bonus’’ bookkeeping the win bonus is often absorbed in the card transfer.

Hence signed zero-sum totals with 100/100 out:

Xmax = 100_card + 100_win + 400_Grand = 600
Ymin = 0_card + 200_out – 400_failedGrand = –200
Xmax – Ymin = 600 – (–200) = 800, i.e. +600/–200.

With 200/100 out:

Xmax = 100 + 100 + 400 = 600
Ymin = 0 + 300 – 400 = –100
Xmax – Ymin = 600 – (–100) = 700, i.e. +600/–100.

In the unsigned cards+Grand Tichu convention that is most often quoted the win is not added separately:

X*_max = 100 + 400 = 500
Y*_min = 200 – 400 = –200 on 100/100 out, X*–Y* = 700
Y*_min = 300 – 400 = –100 on 200/100 out, X*–Y* = 600, the 700 figure being quoted as 500 – (–200).

Colleagues 1,10,11,12,13,15,16,17,18 converge on the 600/–200 signed 800-point family with 100/100 out, and repeatedly note the 700-point 600/–100 variant with the 200/100 order scale. Unresolved for the problem setter: exact order bonus value used – 100+100 = 200 vs 200+100 = 300 – and whether X,Y are signed zero-sum scores or unsigned absolute scores, and whether the 100-point round win is counted separately from the card transfer. The 100-point card ceiling and the 800-point declaration swing are stable; the final numeric X-Y is 800 signed with 100/100 out, 700 signed with 200/100 out, commonly reported as 700 points in the cards+Grand Tichu unsigned convention.
