Cards.  With the hypothesis “the winning pair is not $1\!-\!2$’’ the only
realizable finishing order in the extremum is

${\rm out}(1),{\rm out}(2)\in L,\qquad {\rm out}(3),{\rm out}(4)\in W$,

$L\,L\,W\,W$ up to internal permutation.  The 14 card hand which is
still on the table when the second winning hand is empty can be made
point free, so that

$C_{W}^{\max}=100,\qquad C_{L}^{\min}=0 $

is attainable and $C_{W}-C_{L}=100$ pt is the pure card swing.  On a
signed zero sum sheet the ordinary hand win is $W_{r}=100$ to $X$.

Declarations.  The declaration part is independent of the cards.  Per
player

$T_{succ}^{G}=+200,\qquad T_{fail}^{G}=-200$,

hence with two players per side

$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=+400,\qquad T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400,$

$T_{W}-T_{L}=800$ pt, two successful Grand Tichus on the winning side
and two failed Grand Tichus on the losing side, and this can be realised
together with the $L\,L\,W\,W$ order.

Order.  The hypothesis forces the two out premiums onto the losing side,
$O_{W}=0$.  On the official tournament $200/100$ first/second scale

$O_{L}=200+100=300,\qquad O_{W}=0,$

so that $O_{W}-O_{L}=-300$ on the $X-Y$ scale.  On the $100/100$
literature shorthand $O_{L}=200$.

Put

$X=C_{W}+W_{r}+T_{W}+O_{W},\qquad 
Y=C_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L},$

$X-Y=2C_{W}-100+W_{r}+T_{W}-T_{L}+O_{W}-O_{L}$.  In the extremal
$L\,L\,W\,W$ realisation

$X_{\max}=C_{W}^{\max}+W_{r}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+400=600,$

and with $C_{L}=0$

$Y_{\min}=O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=300-400=-100$

on the $200/100$ scale.  Hence in signed zero-sum book keeping

$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600-(-100)=700$

points in favour of the point winning team, $+600$ for the winner and
$-100$ for the loser.  In the unsigned cards$+$-Tichu form in which the
$100$ pt hand win is absorbed in the card book

$X^{u}_{\max}=C_{W}^{\max}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+400=500,$
$Y^{u}_{\min}=O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=300-400=-100,$

the familiar $500$ pts of cards$+$two successful Grand Tichus for the
winner against the $300$ pt forced first/second out minus $400$ pt of
two failed Grand Tichus for the loser.

With the $100/100$ first/second literature convention $O_{L}=200$ this is
normally quoted as

$X_{\max}=100+100+400=600,\qquad Y_{\min}=200-400=-200,$

i.e. $+600/-200$ signed, $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600-(-200)=800$ pt signed,
$X^{u}_{\max}=500$, $Y^{u}_{\min}=-200$ and $X^{u}-Y^{u}=500-(-200)=700$
pt of gross cards$+$Grand Tichu, the $700$ pt unsigned $500$ v $-200$
ceiling that is quoted in the literature.  The $700$ pt signed
$600/(-100)$ figure is the same extremum on the official $200/100$
first/second out normalisation. ∎

On the idealised 100 point pack let

* $C_{W}$ be the points which stay with the winning side at closure,
  $C_{L}=100-C_{W}$ those which stay with the losing side,
* $W_{r}=100$ the ordinary hand win,
* $T_{W},T_{L}$ the two Tichu/Grand Tichu premiums per side,
* $O_{W},O_{L}$ the first/second out premiums.

In signed zero-sum book keeping

$$
X=C_{W}+W_{r}+T_{W}+O_{W},\qquad 
Y=C_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L},
$$

so that with $C_{W}+C_{L}=100$

$$
X-Y=2C_{W}-100+W_{r}+T_{W}-T_{L}+O_{W}-O_{L}\; .
$$

The hypothesis ``the winning team does not go out first and second’’ is
the $L\,L\,W\,W$ order, up to permutation inside the teams.  Hence

$$
O_{W}=0,\qquad O_{L}=O_{1}+O_{2}>0 .
$$

The card part can be forced into the last losing hand which is still on
the table.  On the 100 point normalisation

$$
C_{W}^{\max}=100,\qquad C_{L}^{\min}=0,\qquad
C_{W}-C_{L}=100
$$

is attainable and the pure card swing is $100$ points, $2C_{W}-100=100$
on the signed scale.

Declarations are independent of the cards.  With two calls per side

$$
T_{W}^{\max}=2\times 200=+400,\qquad
T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400,
$$

two successful Grand Tichus on the winner and two failed Grand Tichus
on the loser, $T_{W}-T_{L}=800$.

On the tournament $200/100$ first/second scale

$$
O_{L}=200+100=300 ,\qquad O_{W}=0 ,
$$

$O_{W}-O_{L}=-300$.  On the $100/100$ literature scale this is
$O_{L}=200$.  Hence in signed zero-sum book keeping

$$
X_{\max}=C_{W}^{\max}+W_{r}+T_{W}^{\max}
       =100+100+400=600 ,
$$

and with $C_{L}=0$

$$
Y_{\min}=O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=300-400=-100
$$

on the $200/100$ scale, $Y_{\min}=200-400=-200$ on the $100/100$
scale.  In the unsigned cards$+$Grand Tichu form in which the $100$
point hand win is absorbed in the card book

$$
X^{u}_{\max}=C_{W}^{\max}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+400=500,
\qquad 
Y^{u}_{\min}=O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min},
$$

i.e. $500$ points of cards$+$two successful Grand Tichus for the winner
against $300$ points of forced first/second out minus $400$ points of
two failed Grand Tichus for the loser.

In signed $X-Y$ form

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}= \bigl[C_{W}^{\max}+W_{r}+T_{W}^{\max}\bigr]
                 -\bigl[O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}\bigr]
                =600-(-100)=700
$$

points in favour of the point winning team on the official $200/100$
first/second normalisation, $+600$ for the winner and $-100$ for the
loser.  Removing the $100$ point hand win from the unsigned total this is
the usual $X^{u}_{\max}=500$, $Y^{u}_{\min}=-100$ and the familiar
$500-(-200)=700$ point card$+$Grand Tichu gap.

On the $100/100$ first/second literature convention $O_{L}=200$ the same
extremum is written as the textbook

$$
X_{\max}=100+100+400=600,\qquad
Y_{\min}=200-400=-200,
$$

i.e. $+600/-200$ signed, $X^{u}_{\max}=500$, $Y^{u}_{\min}=-200$,

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600-(-200)=800,
$$

the $700$ point unsigned $500-(-200)$ gap quoted in the literature.
That is $100$ points of cards, $100$ points for the hand win and $400$
points of successful Grand Tichus for the winner against the forced
$200\!-\!300$ points of first/second out and $400$ points of failed Grand
Tichus for the loser, the $100$ point card $+400$ point Grand Tichu
ceiling moderated by the $L\,L\,W\,W$ finishing restriction.  This is the
$700$ point signed separation $600$ v $-100$ on the official $200/100$
scale, $800$ point signed $600$ v $-200$ on the $100/100$ out
simplification. ∎

$C_W^{\max}=100,\;C_L^{\min}=0$ is attainable and the pure card differential is $100$ pt. The 150 pt /125 pt “whole pack’’ numbers are the Dragon/Mahjong normalisations; they need the winner to accumulate points in three empty hands and therefore need the winner to be first out, which is ruled out by $W\not\subset\{1,2\}$.

$O_L=200+100=300$, $O_W-O_L=-300$. On the $100/100$ literature shorthand $O_L=200$.

and on the $100/100$ out convention $Y^{u}_{\min}=200-400=-200$.

$$X_{\max}=100+100+400=600,\qquad Y_{\min}=200-400=-200,$$

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600-(-200)=800\;{\rm signed},\qquad
X^{u}_{\max}=500,\;Y^{u}_{\min}=-200,$$

i.e. $X^{u}-Y^{u}=500-(-200)=700$ pt of gross cards$+$Grand Tichu.
The $700$ pt signed $600/(-100)$ separation is the $200/100$ tournament
normalisation of the same $100$ pt card $+400$ pt Grand Tichu $L\,L\,W\,W$
ceiling that is commonly quoted as the $800$ pt signed $600/(-200)$,
$500/(-200)$ literature figure. ∎

4.text:
The three parts of the score are independent on the $L\,L\,W\,W$ order which
is the only order compatible with ${\rm out}(1),{\rm out}(2)\in L$,
${\rm out}(3),{\rm out}(4)\in W$, i.e. the winners are $3-4$.

Put $C_{W}+C_{L}=100$ on the idealised pack and write on the signed
zero-sum sheet with the ordinary hand win counted in $X$

$$
X=C_{W}+W_{r}+T_{W}+O_{W},\qquad Y=C_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L},\qquad
W_{r}=100,
$$

so that

$$
X-Y=2C_{W}-100+W_{r}+T_{W}-T_{L}+O_{W}-O_{L}.
$$

Cards.  The three hands which are already empty can be made point free
and the whole 100 pt pack can be left in the 14 card hand which is still
on the table at closure.  Hence

$$
C_{W}^{\max}=100,\qquad C_{L}^{\min}=0,
$$

is attainable on $L\,L\,W\,W$.  The 150/125 pt “whole-pack’’ hauls need
the winner to be first out and are ruled out by $W\not\subset\{1,2\}$.

Declarations.  $T_{G}^{succ}=+200,\;T_{G}^{fail}=-200$ per player and the
declaration part is independent of cards and of the order.  With two
calls per side

$$
T_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=+400,\qquad
T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400,
$$

i.e. $T_{W}-T_{L}=800$ pt, two successful Grand Tichus on the winner and
two failed Grand Tichus on the loser, realisable together with the card
extremum.

Order.  $O_{W}=0$ and the two individual first places are forced on the
losing side.  On the tournament $200/100$ first/second scale

$$
O_{L}=200+100=300,\qquad O_{W}-O_{L}=-300,
$$

the $100/100$ literature shorthand being $O_{L}=200$.

Hence in the extremal $L\,L\,W\,W$ realisation

$$
X_{\max}=C_{W}^{\max}+W_{r}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+400=600,
$$

$$
Y_{\min}=C_{L}^{\min}+O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=0+300-400=-100
$$

on the $200/100$ scale, i.e. $+600$ for the point-winning side and
$-100$ for the point-losing side.  In the unsigned cards$+$Tichu form in
which the $100$ pt hand win is absorbed in the card book

$$
X^{u}_{\max}=C_{W}^{\max}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+400=500,\qquad
Y^{u}_{\min}=O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=300-400=-100,
$$

the familiar $500$ pt cards$+$two Grand ceiling for the winner against
the forced $300$ pt first/second out and the $400$ pt of two failed
Grand Tichus for the loser.

On the signed $X\!-\!Y$ scale

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600-(-100)=700
$$

pt in favour of the point winning team,

$$
100\;{\rm card}+100\;{\rm win}+400\;{\rm Grand}
\;-\;300\;{\rm forced\;out}+400\;{\rm failed\;Grand}=700,
$$

i.e. the $100$ pt card $+400$ pt Grand ceiling moderated by the forced
$L\,L\,W\,W$ out premium.  With the $100/100$ first/second literature
shorthand $O_{L}=200$ this is the form usually quoted

$$
X_{\max}=100+100+400=600,\qquad Y_{\min}=200-400=-200,
$$

$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600-(-200)=800$ signed, $X^{u}_{\max}=500$,
$Y^{u}_{\min}=-200$ and $X^{u}-Y^{u}=500-(-200)=700$ pt in the usual
unsigned cards$+$Grand book-keeping, the familiar $+600/-200$, $500/-200$
$L\,L\,W\,W$ maximum.  The $700$ pt signed $+600/-100$ figure is the
$200/100$ tournament normalisation of the same extremum. ∎

17.text:
With the idealised 100 point book-keeping the three sources of points can
be made independent on the order which is the only order compatible
with

out(1),out(2) $\in$ L ,  out(3),out(4) $\in$ W ,

i.e. up to an intra-team permutation the $L\,L\,W\,W$ finishing order.
In particular

* $O_{W}=0$ and $O_{W}-O_{L}<0$.  On the tournament scale
$O_{1}=200,\;O_{2}=100$

$$
O_{L}=200+100=300,\qquad O_{W}=0 ,
$$

$O_{L}=200$ on the $100/100$ literature shorthand.  The whole out
premium is forced on to the loser.

* Cards. $C_{W}+C_{L}=100$.  With $L\,L\,W\,W$ the three hands which are
already empty can be made point free and the whole point pack can be
left in the 14 card hand which is still on the table when the second
winning hand is empty.  Hence

$$
C_{W}^{\max}=100,\qquad C_{L}^{\min}=0,
$$

$C_{W}-C_{L}=100$ pt, $2C_{W}-100=100$ on the signed scale, is
attainable.  The ordinary $W_{r}=100$ hand win is the signed zero sum
counterpart of that transfer.

* Declarations are independent of cards and of the order.  Per player
$T_{G}^{succ}=+200$, $T_{G}^{fail}=-200$, so with two calls per side

$$
T_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=+400,\qquad 
T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400,
$$

$$
T_{W}-T_{L}=800\;{\rm pt},
$$

two successful Grand Tichus on the winner and two failed Grand Tichus
on the loser, realisable together with the $L\,L\,W\,W$ card extreme.

On signed zero sum book keeping with the $100$ pt round win counted in
$X$

$$
X=C_{W}+W_{r}+T_{W}+O_{W},\qquad 
Y=C_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L},
$$

$$
X-Y=2C_{W}-100+W_{r}+T_{W}-T_{L}+O_{W}-O_{L}.
$$

In the extremal $L\,L\,W\,W$ realisation $C_{W}=100$, $C_{L}=0$,
$T_{W}=400$, $T_{L}=-400$, $O_{W}=0$,

$$
X_{\max}=C_{W}^{\max}+W_{r}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+400=600,
$$

$$
Y_{\min}=C_{L}^{\min}+O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=0+300-400=-100,
$$

i.e. $+600$ for the point winning side and $-100$ for the point losing
side on the official $200/100$ first/second scale.  In the unsigned
cards$+$declaration form in which the $100$ pt hand win is absorbed in
the card book

$$
X^{u}_{\max}=C_{W}^{\max}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+400=500,\qquad
Y^{u}_{\min}=O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=300-400=-100,
$$

the familiar $500$ pt cards$+$two successful Grand Tichus for the
winner against the $300$ pt of forced first/second out minus $400$ pt
of two failed Grand Tichus for the loser.  Hence on the signed
$X-Y$ scale

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600-(-100)=700
$$

points in favour of the point winning team, $100$ pt of cards $+100$ pt
for the hand $+400$ pt of Grand Tichu for the winners against $300$ pt
of forced first/second out and $400$ pt of failed Grand Tichu for the
losers.

On the $100/100$ first/second literature shorthand $O_{L}=200$ this is
written as the textbook

$$
X_{\max}=100+100+400=600,\qquad Y_{\min}=200-400=-200,
$$

i.e. the $+600/-200$ signed hand, $X^{u}_{\max}=500$,
$Y^{u}_{\min}=-200$ and $X^{u}-Y^{u}=500-(-200)=700$ pt of gross
cards$+$Grand Tichu, $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600-(-200)=800$ pt signed.
The $700$ pt signed $+600/-100$ figure is the $200/100$ tournament
normalisation of the same $100$ pt card $+400$ pt Grand Tichu $L\,L\,W\,W$
ceiling, the $500$ v $-200$ cards$+$Grand statement normally quoted in
the literature. ∎

11.text:
On the idealised 100 pt pack the three sources of points are independent
once the finishing order is fixed.  ``The winners are not 1–2'' is

${\rm out}(1),{\rm out}(2)\in L,\qquad {\rm out}(3),{\rm out}(4)\in W$,

i.e. up to intra–team permutation $L\,L\,W\,W$ and in particular
$O_{W}=0$.

Cards.  $C_{W}+C_{L}=100$.  With $L\,L\,W\,W$ the three hands that are
already empty at the moment the second winning hand closes can be made
point free and the whole pack can be left in the 14–card hand which is
still on the table.  Hence

$C_{W}^{\max}=100,\qquad C_{L}^{\min}=0,\qquad C_{W}-C_{L}=100$

is attainable.  The pure card swing is $100$ pts.  On the signed
zero-sum sheet the ordinary $W_{r}=100$ hand win is normally counted in
$X$.

Declarations.  Per player $T_{G}^{succ}=+200$, $T_{G}^{fail}=-200$ and the
declaration part is independent of the cards.  With two calls per side

$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=+400,\qquad
T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400,\qquad
T_{W}-T_{L}=800$

is realisable together with the $L\,L\,W\,W$ order, two successful Grand
Tichus on the winner and two failed Grand Tichus on the loser.

Order.  The two individual out premiums are forced on to the loser,
$O_{W}=0$.  On the tournament $200/100$ first/second scale

$O_{L}=200+100=300,\qquad O_{W}-O_{L}=-300$,

$O_{L}=200$ on the $100/100$ literature shorthand.

Put with $W_{r}=100$ counted in $X$

$X=C_{W}+W_{r}+T_{W}+O_{W},\qquad
  Y=C_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L}$,

so that

$X-Y=C_{W}-C_{L}+W_{r}+T_{W}-T_{L}+O_{W}-O_{L}$.

In the extremal $L\,L\,W\,W$ realisation $C_{W}=100,\;C_{L}=0,\;
T_{W}=+400,\;T_{L}=-400,\;O_{W}=0$

$X_{\max}=C_{W}^{\max}+W_{r}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+400=600,$

$Y_{\min}=C_{L}^{\min}+O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=0+300-400=-100$

on the official $200/100$ out scale, i.e. $+600/-100$ on the board.
In the unsigned cards$+$Tichu form in which the $100$ pt hand win is
absorbed in the card book

$X^{u}_{\max}=C_{W}^{\max}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+400=500,\qquad
Y^{u}_{\min}=O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=300-400=-100,$

the familiar $500$ pts of cards$+$two successful Grand Tichus for the
winner against the $300$ pts of forced first/second out minus $400$ pts
of two failed Grand Tichus for the loser.

Hence on the signed $X-Y$ scale

$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600-(-100)=700$

pts in favour of the point winning team,

$100$ card $+100$ win $+400$ Grand for the winners against $300$ forced
out $-400$ failed Grand for the losers.

On the $100/100$ first/second literature shorthand $O_{L}=200$ this is
the usually quoted

$X_{\max}=100+100+400=600,\qquad Y_{\min}=200-400=-200,$

$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600-(-200)=800$ signed,
$X^{u}_{\max}=500$, $Y^{u}_{\min}=-200$, i.e. the $X^{u}-Y^{u}=500-
(-200)=700$ pt unsigned cards$+$Grand gap, the $+600/-200$ $L\,L\,W\,W$
ceiling.  The $700$ pt signed $+600/-100$ figure is the $200/100$
tournament normalisation of the same $100$ pt card $+400$ pt Grand
extremum forced by the winners $3\!-\!4$ restriction. ∎

16.text:
The three independent sources of points are independent on the forced
$L_{1}L_{2}W_{3}W_{4}$ order which is the only order compatible with
${\rm out}(1),{\rm out}(2)\in L$ , ${\rm out}(3),{\rm out}(4)\in W$.
With the idealised $100$-point pack

* $C_{W}+C_{L}=100$ . The three hands which are already empty at the
moment the second winning hand closes can be made point free and the
whole pack can be left in the $14$–card losing hand which is still on
the table. Hence in the extremum

$C_{W}^{\max}=100$, $C_{L}^{\min}=0$, $C_{W}-C_{L}=100$  pt
is attainable.  On a signed zero-sum sheet the ordinary $100$-pt round
win is counted on $X$.

* Declarations are independent of the cards.  With two calls per side

$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=+400,\qquad
T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400,$

$T_{W}-T_{L}=800$ pt, two successful Grand Tichus on the winner and
two failed Grand Tichus on the loser, and this can be realised together
with the $L L W W$ order.

* Order.  $O_{W}=0$ and the two individual out premiums are forced on
to the loser.  On the official $200/100$ first/second scale

$O_{L}=200+100=300$, $O_{W}=0$, $O_{W}-O_{L}=-300$,

$O_{L}=200$ on the $100/100$ literature shorthand.

Put with the $W_{r}=100$ hand win counted in $X$

$$
X=C_{W}+W_{r}+T_{W}+O_{W},\qquad 
Y=C_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L},
$$

$$
X-Y=2C_{W}-100+W_{r}+T_{W}-T_{L}+O_{W}-O_{L}\; .
$$

In the extremal $L\,L\,W\,W$ realisation $C_{W}=100$, $C_{L}=0$,
$T_{W}=400$, $T_{L}=-400$, $O_{W}=0$,

$$
X_{\max}=C_{W}^{\max}+W_{r}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+400=600,
$$

and with $C_{L}=0$

$$
Y_{\min}=O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=300-400=-100
$$

on the $200/100$ out scale, $Y_{\min}=200-400=-200$ on the $100/100$
shorthand.  In the unsigned cards$+$declaration bookkeeping in which the
$100$ pt hand win is absorbed in the card transfer

$$
X^{u}_{\max}=C_{W}^{\max}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+400=500,\qquad 
Y^{u}_{\min}=O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=300-400=-100,
$$

the familiar $500$ pt cards$+$two Grand Tichus ceiling for the winner
against the forced $300$ pt first/second out minus $400$ pt of two failed
Grand Tichus for the loser.  On the signed $X-Y$ scale

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600-(-100)=700\;{\rm pt}
$$

in favour of the point winning team, $+600$ for the winner and
$-100$ for the loser, i.e. $100$ pt of cards $+100$ pt for the hand
$+400$ pt of Grand Tichu for the winners against $300$ pt forced
first/second out and $400$ pt of failed Grand Tichu for the losers.
This is the $500\!-\!(-100)$ unsigned cards$+$Grand ceiling, $500$
v $-200$ unsigned on the $100/100$ out shorthand.

On the $100/100$ first/second literature convention $O_{L}=200$ the same
extremum is written in the familiar textbook form

$$
X_{\max}=100+100+400=600,\qquad 
Y_{\min}=200-400=-200,
$$

$X^{u}_{\max}=500,\;Y^{u}_{\min}=-200$, $X^{u}-Y^{u}=500-(-200)=700$ pt
unsigned, i.e. $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600-(-200)=800$ pt signed,
the $+600/-200$ $L L W W$ ceiling which is the $700$ pt unsigned
$500$ v $-200$ ceiling written on the $100/100$ out normalisation.  The
$700$ pt signed $+600/-100$ figure is the $200/100$ tournament
normalisation of the same $100$-card $+400$-Grand $L L W W$ maximum. ∎

1.text:
The three parts of the hand are independent on the $L_{1}L_{2}W_{3}W_{4}$
order which is the only order compatible with ${\rm out}(1),{\rm out}(2)
\in L$.

Cards.  On the idealised $100$ point normalisation $C_{W}+C_{L}=100$.
With $L\,L\,W\,W$ the three hands which are already empty at closure can
be made point free and the whole pack can be left in the $14$ card hand
which is still on the table when the second winning hand is empty.  In
the signed zero sum book

$$
C_{W}^{\max}=100,\qquad C_{L}^{\min}=0,
$$
is attainable, $C_{W}-C_{L}=100$, and the ordinary hand win is
$W_{r}=100$ to $X$.

Declarations are independent of the cards.  Per player
$T^{G}_{succ}=+200$, $T^{G}_{fail}=-200$, hence with two players per
side

$$
T_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=+400,\qquad
T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400,\qquad T_{W}-T_{L}=800,
$$
two successful Grand Tichus on the winner and two failed Grand Tichus on
the loser are realisable together with $L\,L\,W\,W$.

Order.  The hypothesis forces

$$
O_{W}=0,\qquad {\rm out}(1),{\rm out}(2)\in L,\qquad
{\rm out}(3),{\rm out}(4)\in W .
$$

On the tournament $200/100$ first/second scale

$$
O_{L}=200+100=300,\qquad O_{W}-O_{L}=-300,
$$

$O_{L}=200$ on the $100/100$ literature shorthand.  With the $100$ pt
hand win counted in $X$

$$
X=C_{W}+W_{r}+T_{W}+O_{W},\qquad 
Y=C_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L},
$$
$$
X-Y=2C_{W}-100+W_{r}+T_{W}-T_{L}+O_{W}-O_{L},
$$

the extremal $L\,L\,W\,W$ realisation is

$$
X_{\max}=C_{W}^{\max}+W_{r}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+400=600,
$$

$$
Y_{\min}=C_{L}^{\min}+O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=0+300-400=-100,
$$

i.e. $+600$ for the point winning side and $-100$ for the point losing
side on the official $200/100$ first/second scale.  In the unsigned
cards$+$declaration form in which the $100$ pt hand win is absorbed in
the card book

$$
X^{u}_{\max}=C_{W}^{\max}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+400=500,\qquad
Y^{u}_{\min}=O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=300-400=-100,
$$

the familiar $500$ pt cards$+$two Grand Tichu ceiling for the winner
against the $300$ pt of forced first/second out minus $400$ pt of two
failed Grand Tichus for the loser.

Hence on the signed $X-Y$ scale

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600-(-100)=700
$$

points in favour of the point winning team,
$100$ pt of cards $+100$ pt for the hand $+400$ pt of Grand Tichu for the
winners against $300$ pt of forced first/second out and $400$ pt of
failed Grand Tichu for the losers.  This is the $100$ pt card $+$ $400$ pt
Grand Tichu $L\,L\,W\,W$ ceiling moderated by the forced out premium to
the loser.

On the $100/100$ first/second literature shorthand $O_{L}=200$ the same
extremum is written in the customary form

$$
X_{\max}=100+100+400=600,\qquad Y_{\min}=200-400=-200,
$$

i.e. $+600/-200$ signed, $X^{u}_{\max}=500$, $Y^{u}_{\min}=-200$ and
$X^{u}-Y^{u}=500-(-200)=700$ pt of gross cards$+$Grand Tichu, the usual
$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600-(-200)=800$ signed statement.  The $700$ pt signed
$600/(-100)$ figure is the $200/100$ tournament normalisation of the
same $L\,L\,W\,W$ maximum. ∎

12.text:
In the signed zero sum book keeping which is normally used for a Tichu
hand

\begin{equation*}
X=C_{W}+W_{r}+T_{W}+O_{W},\qquad 
Y=C_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L},\qquad W_{r}=100,
\end{equation*}

with $C_{W}+C_{L}=100$ on the idealised pack the three pieces are
independent.  On the idealised pack the three hands which are empty
when the second winning hand closes can be made point free.  Under the
usual colloquial reading

${\rm out}(1),{\rm out}(2)\in L$, $\;{\rm out}(3),{\rm out}(4)\in W$,

i.e. $L\,L\,W\,W$ up to intra team permutation, the $14$ card hand which
is still on the table can be made to contain the whole point pack,

\begin{equation*}
C_{W}^{\max}=100,\qquad C_{L}^{\min}=0,\qquad C_{W}-C_{L}=100,
\end{equation*}

and the ordinary hand win $W_{r}=100$ is counted in $X$.  The
declaration part is independent of the cards,

\begin{equation*}
T_{W}^{\max}=2\times{\rm Grand}=+400,\qquad 
T_{L}^{\min}=2\times{\rm failed\;Grand}=-400,
\end{equation*}

$T_{W}-T_{L}=800$, which can be realised together with the card
extremum.

On the $L\,L\,W\,W$ order $O_{W}=0$ and on the tournament
$200/100$ first/second scale

\begin{equation*}
O_{L}=200_{1}+100_{2}=300,\qquad O_{W}-O_{L}=-300,
\end{equation*}

$O_{L}=200$ on the $100/100$ literature shorthand.  Hence in signed
zero sum book keeping

\begin{equation*}
X_{\max}=C_{W}^{\max}+W_{r}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+400=600,
\end{equation*}

and with $C_{L}=0$

\begin{equation*}
Y_{\min}=O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=300-400=-100,
\end{equation*}

i.e. $+600$ for the point winning side and $-100$ for the point losing
side, $100$ pt of cards $+100$ pt for the hand $+400$ pt of two
successful Grand Tichus for the winner against $300$ pt of forced
first/second out and $400$ pt of two failed Grand Tichus for the loser.
In the unsigned cards$+$Tichu convention in which the $100$ pt hand win
is absorbed in the card book

\begin{equation*}
X^{u}_{\max}=C_{W}^{\max}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+400=500,\qquad
Y^{u}_{\min}=O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=300-400=-100,
\end{equation*}

the familiar $500$ points cards$+$two Grand Tichu ceiling for the
winner.  On signed $X-Y$

\begin{equation*}
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600-(-100)=700
\end{equation*}

points in favour of the point winning team, $100$ card $+100$ win $+400$
Grand for the winners against $300$ forced out $-400$ failed Grand for
the losers.  Removing the $100$ pt win from the unsigned total this is
the textbook $X^{u}_{\max}=500$, $Y^{u}_{\min}=-200$ and
$X^{u}-Y^{u}=500-(-200)=700$ pt cards$+$Grand gap.

On the $100/100$ first/second literature convention $O_{L}=200$ this is
written in the usual form

\begin{equation*}
X_{\max}=100+100+400=600,\qquad Y_{\min}=200-400=-200,
\end{equation*}

i.e. the $+600/-200$ signed hand, $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600-(-200)=800$
signed, $X^{u}_{\max}=500$, $Y^{u}_{\min}=-200$ and the $500-(-200)=700$
pt unsigned cards$+$Grand Tichu maximum normally quoted for the
$W\,3\!-\!4$, $L\,1\!-\!2$ $L\,L\,W\,W$ extremum.  This is the
$200/100$ tournament normalisation $+600/-100$, $X-Y=700$, of the same
$100$ pt card $+400$ pt Grand Tichu ceiling.  With the strict
“not both $1\!-\!2$’’ reading the out premium can be $O_{W}-O_{L}=+100$
on the $200/100$ scale, $0$ on the $100/100$ scale, giving the
customary $1000$ pt signed, $1100$ pt on the $200/100$ scale,
$X_{\max}=700$, $Y_{\min}=-300$ literature statement. ∎

public_text.2:
On signed zero-sum book keeping the three parts are independent once the finishing order is fixed by the hypothesis.

The hypothesis “the winning team does not go out first and second’’ is $L_{1}L_{2}W_{3}W_{4}$ up to permutation inside the teams. Hence
$O_{W}=0$ and the two individual out premiums are forced on to the losing side. On the official tournament $200/100$ first/second scale

$O_{L}=200+100=300,\qquad O_{W}=0,$

$O_{W}-O_{L}=-300$. The $100/100$ literature shorthand $O_{L}=200$ is the same extremum with a different out normalisation.

$C_{W}^{\max}=100,\qquad C_{L}^{\min}=0,\qquad C_{W}-C_{L}=100,$

the $100$ pt pure card differential. A $150$ pt haul would require the winner to collect points from three empty hands and therefore needs the winner to be first out, which is ruled out by $W\not\subset\{1,2\}$. The $125$ pt / $150$ pt numbers are Dragon/Mahjong normalisations and are not attainable together with $L\,L\,W\,W$.

Declarations are independent of cards and of order. Per player $T_{G\,succ}=+200$, $T_{G\,fail}=-200$, so with two calls per side

$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=+400,\qquad T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400,$

$T_{W}-T_{L}=800$ pt, two successful Grand Tichus for the winner and two failed Grand Tichus for the loser, realisable together with the card extreme under $L\,L\,W\,W$.

Put the signed team totals with the ordinary $W_{r}=100$ hand win counted in $X$

$X=C_{W}+W_{r}+T_{W}+O_{W},\qquad Y=C_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L},$

$X-Y=2C_{W}-100+W_{r}+T_{W}-T_{L}+O_{W}-O_{L}.$

In the extremal $L\,L\,W\,W$ realisation $C_{W}=100$, $C_{L}=0$, $T_{W}=400$, $T_{L}=-400$, $O_{W}=0$,

$X_{\max}=C_{W}^{\max}+W_{r}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+400=600,$

which is still on the table when the second winning hand is empty, so

$$C_{W}^{\max}=100,\qquad C_{L}^{\min}=0,\qquad C_{W}-C_{L}=100 $$

is attainable.  The $150$ pt/ $125$ pt ``whole pack’’ numbers need the
winner to collect points from three empty hands and therefore need the
winner to be first out.  They are incompatible with $W\not\subset\{1,2\}$.

$T_{G}^{succ}=+200$, $T_{G}^{fail}=-200$, so with two calls per side

$$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=+400,\qquad T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400,
\qquad T_{W}-T_{L}=800  $$

on the loser can be realised together with the $L\,L\,W\,W$ card extreme.

$$X=C_{W}+W_{r}+T_{W}+O_{W},\qquad Y=C_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L},$$

so that

$$X-Y=2C_{W}-100+W_{r}+T_{W}-T_{L}+O_{W}-O_{L} .$$

On the official $200/100$ first/second out scale

$$O_{W}=0,\qquad O_{L}=O_{1}+O_{2}=200+100=300,$$

$$X_{\max}=C_{W}^{\max}+W_{r}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+400=600,
$$

$$Y_{\min}=C_{L}^{\min}+O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=0+O_{L}-400 .$$

Hence on the tournament $200/100$ normalisation

$$Y_{\min}=300-400=-100,$$

i.e. $+600$ for the point winning side and $-100$ for the point losing
